docs.title: sp_segment
docs.text:
sp_segment is a Nextflow pipeline that segments cells in multiplex spatial proteomics images from COMET, MIBI and OPAL. It writes one GeoJSON file per image that contains every cell outline and its measurements. You can open the GeoJSON in QuPath.

For each image, the pipeline can:

  • subtract background (COMET only)
  • segment whole cells, and optionally nuclei, with Cellpose, Mesmer or CellSAM
  • smooth the label masks
  • measure shape and per-channel intensity for each cell compartment
  • add a 768-value KRONOS2 embedding to every cell
  • write an HTML QC report

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
Dashed boxes are optional steps. Nuclear segmentation is optional for every method and is off by default (use_whole_cell_only = true).

flowchart TD
  input["Multiplex TIFF"] --> extract["Extract markers"]
  extract --> bgsub["Background subtraction"]
  bgsub --> combine["Combine membrane channels"]
  input --> combine
  combine --> choose{"Segmentation method"}

  choose -- Cellpose --> convert["sopa convert"]
  convert --> patchify["sopa patchify"]
  patchify --> cellpose["Cellpose on each patch"]
  cellpose --> resolve["sopa resolve"]
  resolve --> totiff["Parquet to TIFF"]
  totiff --> smooth["Smooth masks"]

  choose -- Mesmer --> mesmer["Mesmer"]
  mesmer --> smooth

  choose -- CellSAM --> cellsam["CellSAM"]
  cellsam --> smooth

  smooth --> measure["Cell measurement"]
  measure --> geojson["GeoJSON"]
  measure --> kronos["KRONOS2 embeddings"]
  kronos --> kgeojson["GeoJSON with embeddings"]
  kronos --> markers["Marker report"]
  measure --> report["Segmentation report"]

  style extract stroke-dasharray: 5 5
  style bgsub stroke-dasharray: 5 5
  style smooth stroke-dasharray: 5 5
  style kronos stroke-dasharray: 5 5
  style report stroke-dasharray: 5 5

docs.text:

docs.text: The format is based on Keep a Changelog and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• :warning: use_whole_cell_only now defaults to true. Nuclei are not segmented or measured unless --use_whole_cell_only false is set. Runs that need nuclear masks or nuclear measurements must set it.
  • :warning: cellpose_min_area now defaults to 100 (was 200). Cellpose keeps cells from 100 to 199 pixels² that were removed before. Set --cellpose_min_area 200 to match earlier results. cellsam_min_area still defaults to 200.
  • The Mask smoothing options and Cellpose preprocessing options parameters are hidden in --help and the Seqera Platform launch form. Show them with --show_hidden. They can still be set, and their defaults are unchanged.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• combine_method norm_mean for Cellpose and CellSAM. Each membrane channel is rescaled to its own 50th–99.5th percentile, then the channels are averaged, so a dim marker is not hidden by a bright one. max stays the default. A sample that runs Mesmer with norm_mean and more than one membrane channel stops the run at startup, because mesmer-segment has only max.
  • cellsam_remove_border_cells (default true). Set it to false to keep CellSAM cells that touch the image edge. Border cells were previously always removed.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • combine_method prod. Setting --combine_method prod fails at startup.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• :warning: Background subtraction could use another sample's markers file. With two or more run_backsub samples in one run, an image could be corrected with another slide's exposure times and background channels. Re-run background subtraction for runs with more than one backsub sample.
  • extract_markers could give a marker another channel's background channel or exposure time when the OME-XML lists ChannelPriv elements in a different order from the channels, or stores one channel per Image. Output for standard COMET files is unchanged.
  • The samplesheet is checked before any task runs. Sample names must be unique; a row can set at most one of run_mesmer, run_cellpose and run_cellsam; a row must run something; segmentation rows need nuclear_channel and membrane_channels. These cases previously overwrote outputs, dropped samples or crashed.
  • Channel names can contain any character except ", ', : and ,, and names with spaces are passed correctly to every tool.
  • combine_channels reads images that store one channel per OME Image (COMET _fixed exports), panels with a repeated channel name, and TIFFs with a plain JSON description. It reads only the nuclear and membrane channels and writes valid OME-XML.
  • CellSAM fails when it finds no cells instead of writing an empty mask. The whole-cell and nuclear tasks no longer race on the shared model download.
  • An invalid kronos_marker_mapping (not an existing file and not valid JSON) fails the run. A mapping file is staged into the container, so relative paths work. Mapping entries that match no channel are listed in the marker report. enable_kronos without kronos_model_path fails at startup.
  • software_versions.yml lists every tool. CellSAM and Mesmer versions are read from the installed packages instead of being hardcoded.
  • Cellpose resolve and measurement for a sample start when that sample's patches finish, instead of after every sample's patches.
  • GPU tasks get --nv under Apptainer or Singularity with any profile. sopa Cellpose previously ran on CPU unless a small, medium, large or wehi_* profile was used.
  • The test profiles read their samplesheets from the pipeline directory.
  • KRONOS2, Mesmer and CellSAM no longer need a writable home directory inside the container. They failed with Read-only file system when the home directory was not mounted. Without deepcell_cache_dir, Mesmer and CellSAM now keep their model files in the task directory in that case.
  • deepcell_cache_dir is created if it does not exist. Previously every Mesmer and CellSAM task failed to start until it was created by hand.
  • nf-test snapshots updated for Mesmer, CellSAM, Cellpose, cell measurement and their subworkflows. 37 of 38 tests pass. Snapshot entries for tests that no longer exist were removed.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Added a documentation site built with MkDocs Material, deployed to GitHub Pages with versions per release.
  • The parameter and samplesheet references are generated from the JSON schemas by docs/scripts/generate_reference.py.
  • nextflow_schema.json now lists the default of every parameter that has one in nextflow.config, and its help text is corrected.
  • Added docs/background/membrane-channels.md: how membrane channels are combined, and how max and norm_mean compared.
  • Added docs/background/tiling-and-straight-edges.md: where straight cell edges come from (CellSAM block stitching, sopa patch stitching, the Cellpose-SAM network output) and the tests of fixes.
  • Removed the KRONOS2 migration working notes and the unused docs/examples/additional_markers.csv.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• :warning: Label masks are always uint32 (were uint16). Masks with more than 65,535 cells were silently truncated: every cell past 65,535 was merged into low label IDs. Regenerate any mask with more than 65,535 cells made by an earlier version. Masks with fewer cells are unchanged. cellsam_segment.py fails if the cell count exceeds uint32.
  • Intermediate label masks (PARQUETTOTIFF, CELLSAMSEGMENT) are written with deflate compression. A dense whole-slide mask fell from 2.87 GB to 31 MB. The smoothed mask is still uncompressed.
  • neighbors defaults to 0 (disabled). It was 5.
  • Resource profiles: small, medium and large are unchanged. New WEHI Milton profiles wehi_small, wehi_med and wehi_large request most of a node, for samples with many cells.
  • cellmeasurement-py updated to 0.2.2 (faster GeoJSON export overlap step) via 0.2.1 (fixes channel detection on OPAL OME-TIFFs).
  • :warning: Cellpose preprocessing now matches Cellpose: sopa's gaussian filter and CLAHE are off. New parameters cellpose_clip_limit (0), cellpose_gaussian_sigma (0), cellpose_clahe_kernel_size (unset) and cellpose_tile_norm_blocksize (0). Restore the old behaviour with --cellpose_clip_limit 0.2 --cellpose_gaussian_sigma 1. Results no longer depend strongly on patch_width_pixel: cells keeping the same outline (IoU ≥ 0.90) when the patch width changes rose from 37-43% to 82-87%. Results change: median cell area falls 23-43% and cell counts change by -10% to +54% depending on the model. Do not pool Cellpose results from before and after this version.
  • The Singularity and Apptainer image pull timeout is 1 hour (was 20 minutes). CI caches the converted images.
  • :warning: cellsam_min_area defaults to 200 (was 0), the same as cellpose_min_area. CellSAM objects smaller than 200 pixels² are removed. Set --cellsam_min_area 0 for the old behaviour. Do not pool CellSAM results from before and after this version.
  • The Cellpose parameter descriptions state which direction finds more cells.
  • New parameter container_cache_dir puts converted container images on a path of your choice. If it is set while APPTAINER_CACHEDIR is under $HOME, the pipeline stops at startup. If the layer cache is under $HOME, it warns.
  • deepcell_cache_dir is mounted into the Mesmer and CellSAM containers. Before, the weights were downloaded again in every task.
  • Cellpose updated to 4.2.1.1 (sopa 2.2.6) and runs on the GPU. With the model fixed, the update does not change results.
  • cellpose_pretrained_model selects the model and defaults to cpsam_v2 (was unset). It accepts cpsam_v2, cpsam, cpdino, cpdino-vitb or a path to a custom model.
  • cellpose_model_type is removed and setting it is an error. Cellpose 4 ignored it, so runs that set cyto3 used cpsam.
  • Cellpose weights are downloaded once per run by the new CELLPOSEMODEL process, not once per patch task. This fixes HTTP 429 errors.
  • A missing custom Cellpose model path or cellpose_models_dir stops the pipeline at startup. Before, Cellpose used its built-in weights without warning.
  • The nf-test snapshot suite was repaired, including sopa_patchifyimage - zarr and the backgroundsubtract snapshot (which no longer records the output md5, because the file contains a new UUID on every run).
  • KRONOS1 is replaced by KRONOS2. Embeddings have 768 values (were 384). KRONOS1 and KRONOS2 embeddings cannot be compared.
  • KRONOS2 runs once at the top level, not inside each segmentation subworkflow.
  • KRONOS2 patches contain only the target cell: pixels outside the cell are set to 0. Disable with --kronos_isolate_cell false.
  • The KRONOS2 intensity divisor is derived from the image data type (uint8 255, uint16 65535, float 400). Float images were divided by 65535 before.
  • The samplesheet nuclear_channel is passed to KRONOS2 as its DAPI channel, so DRAQ5 and Hoechst slides get DAPI statistics.
  • kronos_batch_size defaults to 16 (was 32), which reproduces the published values.
  • The per-cell embeddings CSV is no longer written. Embeddings are in the cell measurement GeoJSON.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• geometry_checkpoint_dir and geometry_batch_size (default 2000): a CELLMEASUREMENT task killed during polygon extraction resumes from the last completed batch. The directory must be outside the work directory.
  • kronos_exclude_markers: channels KRONOS2 does not read, for channels that are not markers (for example autofluorescence). Other steps still use them. Excluding a channel changes every cell's embedding.
  • The cpdino and cpdino-vitb Cellpose models work. The container includes Meta's dinov3 code. See CITATIONS.md for the licence.
  • cellpose_models_dir: a directory of pre-downloaded Cellpose weights.
  • CELLPOSE_MODELS_DIR environment variable for nf-test runs (tests/nextflow.config).
  • bin/kronos2_common.py, shared code for per-cell foundation-model embeddings.
  • KRONOS2 container pinned by digest (community.wave.seqera.io/library/kronos2embeddings:70590359503eec08, torch 2.6.0+cu124).
  • kronos_nuclear_marker, kronos_isolate_cell and kronos_allow_novel_defaults parameters, and the test_mesmer_kronos2 profile.
  • KRONOS2 fails by default when a channel name is not in its vocabulary. Fix with kronos_marker_mapping, or accept default statistics with kronos_allow_novel_defaults.
  • KRONOS2 cell footprints are drawn with Pillow instead of rasterio. Embeddings change by a cosine similarity of 0.99974.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• kronos_marker_metadata: KRONOS2 has its own 288-marker vocabulary.
  • kronos_config_path: KRONOS2 has no config file.
  • kronos_distance_threshold: cells are joined to embeddings by GeoJSON feature order.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• :warning: KRONOS2 read only the first channel of OME-TIFFs that store each channel as its own series (for example COMET _fixed exports), and used it for every marker. Regenerate embeddings made from such images by earlier versions. The pipeline now reads each channel from its own series and fails if the channel count and the name count differ.
  • A channel with neither an OME Name nor an ID shifted every later marker onto the wrong channel in KRONOS2. Names are now assigned by position.
  • Stub runs of the Cellpose path failed with For input string: "".
  • The KRONOS2 module passed --nv under Docker. It now passes --nv or --gpus all according to the container engine.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• cellmeasurement: the Python implementation (cellmeasurement-py) replaces the Groovy one.
  • cellmeasurement: measurements are computed on tiles in parallel. Tile size and overlap are configurable.
  • cellmeasurement: erosion measurements use 5 equal-area rings named <channel>: <compartment>: ErosionBin_<N>: Mean and Median. The Groovy names (Eroded_<N>px) are no longer produced.
  • cellmeasurement: --erosion-steps is a boolean and no longer takes pixel depths.
  • The pipeline can run with whole-cell segmentation only.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• KRONOS embeddings (kronosembeddings module, 384 values per cell), disabled by default. Replaced by KRONOS2 in v0.5.0.
  • CellSAM segmentation (cellsam_segment), with cellsam_bbox_threshold, cellsam_block_size, cellsam_overlap, cellsam_iou_threshold and cellsam_use_wsi.
  • Mask smoothing (smooth_masks, smooth_method, smooth_kernel_size) with the morphological and shapely methods.
  • dist_threshold (default 10.0) and downsample_factor (default 1.0) cell measurement parameters.

docs.text:
• Background_subtraction

Background subtraction for COMET images, from the Schapiro lab. Cite the repository.

  • Cellpose

Stringer C, Wang T, Michaelos M, Pachitariu M. Cellpose: a generalist algorithm for cellular segmentation. Nat Methods. 2021 Jan;18(1):100-106. doi: 10.1038/s41592-020-01018-x.

The default models (cpsam_v2, cpsam) are Cellpose-SAM:

Pachitariu M, Rariden M, Stringer C. Cellpose-SAM: superhuman generalization for cellular segmentation. bioRxiv. 2025.

  • sopa

Blampey Q, Mulder K, Gardet M, Christodoulidis S, Dutertre CA, André F, Ginhoux F, Cournède PH. Sopa: a technology-invariant pipeline for analyses of image-based spatial omics. Nat Commun. 2024;15:4981. doi: 10.1038/s41467-024-48981-z.

  • Mesmer, run through MesmerSegmentation

Greenwald NF, Miller G, Moen E, Kong A, Kagel A, Dougherty T, et al. Whole-cell segmentation of tissue images with human-level performance using large-scale data annotation and deep learning. Nat Biotechnol. 2022;40(4):555-565. doi: 10.1038/s41587-021-01094-0.

  • CellSAM

Israel U, Marks M, Dilip R, Li Q, Yu C, Laubscher E, et al. CellSAM: a foundation model for cell segmentation. bioRxiv. 2023.

  • KRONOS2

Foundation model for multiplex spatial proteomics, from the Mahmood lab. Cite the publication listed on the model card.

  • cellmeasurement-py

Cell matching and measurement, from the WEHI SODA Hub.

  • spatialVis

R package used for the segmentation report, from the WEHI SODA Hub.

  • DINOv3

Used only by the cpdino and cpdino-vitb Cellpose models, which build a DINOv3 backbone architecture and load Cellpose's own fine-tuned weights. Meta's pretrained backbone weights are not used and are not required.

DINOv3 is distributed under the DINOv3 License. The pipeline's Cellpose container redistributes the DINOv3 code, so a copy of the DINOv3 License Agreement must accompany that container, and work published using these models must acknowledge the DINOv3 materials. See the licence for the full terms, including its acceptable-use restrictions.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Nextflow 24.04.2 or later.
  • A container engine: Apptainer, Singularity or Docker. Conda is not supported.
  • A GPU for Cellpose, CellSAM and KRONOS2. These steps request one GPU per task (the process_gpu label). Mesmer, background subtraction and cell measurement run on CPU.
  • A DeepCell access token for Mesmer. CellSAM uses it if present. See Secrets.

If you are new to Nextflow, see the nf-core installation guide.

docs.title: Get the pipeline
docs.text:
Nextflow downloads the pipeline the first time you run it. To download or update it without running:

nextflow pull WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment

Use -r to run a fixed release, for example -r 0.5.0. Releases are listed on the releases page. Record the release you used so the run can be repeated.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Mesmer downloads its model from DeepCell and needs an access token. Create one at users.deepcell.org, then store it as a Nextflow secret:

nextflow secrets set DEEPCELL_ACCESS_TOKEN <your-token>

CellSAM uses the same secret to download the CellSAM v1.2 weights. Without it, CellSAM uses its default weights.

docs.title: Test profiles
docs.text:
Each test profile runs a small synthetic COMET image (tests/data/comet/synthetic_multichannel.tif). Combine a test profile with a container profile, for example -profile test,singularity.

Profile Method Background subtraction Notes test Cellpose yes This is the profile CI runs. test_no_backsub Cellpose no test_multisample Cellpose and Mesmer Mesmer sample only Three samples: two Cellpose, one Mesmer. test_mesmer Mesmer yes Needs DEEPCELL_ACCESS_TOKEN. test_mesmer_no_backsub Mesmer no Needs DEEPCELL_ACCESS_TOKEN. Currently fails: see below. test_mesmer_kronos2 Mesmer yes Also runs KRONOS2. Set KRONOS2_MODEL_DIR to a KRONOS2 snapshot. test_cellsam CellSAM yes test_cellsam_no_backsub CellSAM no

The test samplesheets give image paths relative to the repository root, so run the test profiles from the root of a clone:

git clone https://github.com/WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment.git
cd sp_segment
nextflow run . -profile test_cellsam,singularity --outdir results

The test profiles limit each task to 4 CPUs, 15 GB of memory and 1 hour.

test_mesmer_no_backsub fails with PhysicalSizeX or PhysicalSizeY not found in the XML. Mesmer needs the pixel size in the OME-XML, and the synthetic test image has none. Background subtraction adds it, so test_mesmer passes.

docs.title: First run on your data
docs.text:
Write a samplesheet with one row per image. See Samplesheet for every column.

sample,run_backsub,run_cellpose,tiff,nuclear_channel,membrane_channels
slide1,true,true,/data/slide1.ome.tiff,DAPI,CD45:Pan-Cytokeratin

Run the pipeline:

nextflow run WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment \
    -r 0.5.0 \
    -profile singularity \
    --input samplesheet.csv \
    --outdir results

The cells are in results/cellmeasurement/slide1.geojson.gz. See View results in QuPath.

To run on a Slurm cluster, add a resource profile such as medium. See Resource profiles. For all run options, see Running the pipeline.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: All paths are relative to --outdir. <sample> is the sample value from the samplesheet. Which directories appear depends on the steps each sample runs.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Directory Written when Main files extractmarkers/ run_backsub = true <sample>_markers.csv backsub/ run_backsub = true <sample>.ome.tif, markers CSV combinechannels/ any segmentation <sample>_combined_channels.tiff sopa/ Cellpose <sample>.zarr parquettotiff/ Cellpose <sample>_whole-cell.tiff, <sample>_nuclear.tiff mesmerwc/, mesmernuc/ Mesmer <sample>_whole-cell.tiff, <sample>_nuclear.tiff cellsamwc/, cellsamnuc/ CellSAM <sample>_whole-cell.tiff, <sample>_nuclear.tiff smoothmasks/ smooth_masks = true *_smoothed.tiff cellmeasurement/ any segmentation <sample>.geojson.gz, <sample>_mask.tiff kronos2embeddings/ enable_kronos = true <sample>_marker_report.txt segmentationreport/ generate_report = true <sample>/<sample>.html pipeline_info/ always Nextflow reports, software versions

Nuclear masks (*_nuclear.tiff, mesmernuc/, cellsamnuc/) are written only when use_whole_cell_only = false.

docs.title: Background subtraction
docs.text:
COMET only.

  • extractmarkers/<sample>_markers.csv: one row per channel with the marker name, its background channel and its exposure time, read from the OME-XML.
  • backsub/<sample>.ome.tif: the background-subtracted image. Channels in remove_markers (default TRITC,Cy5) are removed.

When a sample also runs segmentation, the segmentation uses this image.

docs.title: Combined channels
docs.text: • combinechannels/<sample>_combined_channels.tiff: a two-channel image with the nuclear channel and the membrane channels combined into one with combine_method. This is the image each segmentation method reads.

docs.title: Segmentation masks
docs.text:
Each mask is a TIFF in which every cell has its own integer label and the background is 0. Masks are uint32, so images with more than 65,535 cells are supported.

  • Cellpose: parquettotiff/<sample>_whole-cell.tiff and parquettotiff/<sample>_nuclear.tiff. sopa/<sample>.zarr holds the SpatialData store with the image patches and the Cellpose cell boundaries.
  • Mesmer: mesmerwc/<sample>_whole-cell.tiff and mesmernuc/<sample>_nuclear.tiff.
  • CellSAM: cellsamwc/<sample>_whole-cell.tiff and cellsamnuc/<sample>_nuclear.tiff. CellSAM fails the task if the mask contains no cells.

docs.title: Smoothed masks
docs.text: When smooth_masks = true, smoothmasks/ holds a smoothed copy of each mask, named after the input mask with _smoothed.tiff added, for example <sample>_whole-cell_smoothed.tiff. Cell measurement then uses the smoothed masks. See smooth_method in Parameters.

docs.title: Cell measurement
docs.text:
• cellmeasurement/<sample>.geojson.gz: one GeoJSON feature per cell, with the cell outline, the nucleus outline when nuclei were segmented, and the measurements. With gzip_geojson = false the file is <sample>.geojson.
  • cellmeasurement/<sample>_mask.tiff: the final cell label mask, rasterised from the cells in the GeoJSON.

docs.title: Measurement names
docs.text:
Measurements use QuPath-style names: <channel>: <compartment>: <statistic>.

Measurement Example Written when Intensity per compartment CD45: Cell: Mean enable_measurements = true Intensity percentile CD45: Cell: Percentile: 95 percentiles is set Erosion ring (1-5, boundary inward) CD45: Cell: ErosionBin_1: Mean erosion_steps = true Expansion ring (1-5, up to 20 µm outward) CD45: Cell: ExpansionBin_3: Median expansion_steps = true 20 µm environment zone CD45: Cell: Environment_20um: Std.Dev. environment_expansion = true Shape Cell: Area µm^2, Cell: Solidity enable_measurements = true Neighbourhood mean Neighbours: Mean: CD45: Cell: Mean neighbors > 0 KRONOS2 embedding (768 values) kronos_emb_0 to kronos_emb_767 enable_kronos = true
  • Intensity statistics are Mean, Median, Min, Max and Std.Dev.. Erosion and expansion rings have Mean and Median only.
  • Compartments are Cell, Nucleus, Cytoplasm and Membrane. Nucleus measurements are written only when use_whole_cell_only = false.
  • Shape measurements are Area µm^2, Circularity, Length µm, Max diameter µm, Min diameter µm and Solidity, for Cell and, with nuclei, Nucleus. With nuclei, Nucleus/Cell area ratio is also written.
  • Distances and areas in µm use pixel_size_microns (default 0.28).

docs.title: KRONOS2 embeddings
docs.text:
When enable_kronos = true:

  • cellmeasurement/<sample>.geojson.gz is replaced by a copy with 768 kronos_emb_* measurements added to every cell. Embedding row i belongs to cell feature i. Running KRONOS2 again on the same file replaces the kronos_emb_* values.
  • kronos2embeddings/<sample>_marker_report.txt lists, for each channel, the name given to KRONOS2, any mapping applied, any channel left out with kronos_exclude_markers, any name not in the KRONOS2 vocabulary, and any kronos_marker_mapping entry that matches no channel. The first line gives the number of channels KRONOS2 used. The report is written even when the run fails on an unmatched marker.

768 numbers per cell make the GeoJSON much larger. Keep gzip_geojson = true (the default).

docs.title: Segmentation report
docs.text:
When generate_report = true:

  • segmentationreport/<sample>/<sample>.html: a QC report for the sample. It is most complete with enable_measurements = true.

docs.title: Pipeline information
docs.text:
pipeline_info/ contains:

  • Nextflow reports: execution_report_<timestamp>.html, execution_timeline_<timestamp>.html, execution_trace_<timestamp>.txt and pipeline_dag_<timestamp>.html.
  • nf_core_pipeline_software_versions.yml: the version of every tool used.
  • params_<timestamp>.json: the parameters of the run.
  • pipeline_report.html and pipeline_report.txt, only when --email or --email_on_fail is set.

The Nextflow reports show the run time, CPU and memory use of every task, which helps when choosing resources.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Find the failing task in the Nextflow log, then look in its work directory (shown in the error) at .command.err, .command.out and .command.log.

docs.title: Results look wrong
docs.text:
• Cells appear flipped or rotated relative to the image (Mesmer): set --mesmer_transpose_mask true.
  • Measurements show only one channel's values for every marker: check that the channel names in the image are what you expect. Images that store each channel as its own OME series (for example COMET _fixed exports) were read incorrectly by some steps of earlier versions.
  • Masks from versions before 0.5.0 with more than 65,535 cells are truncated. Regenerate them.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text: Open an issue on GitHub with the command you ran, the Nextflow version, the pipeline version, and the .command.err of the failing task.

docs.title: Basic command
docs.text:
nextflow run WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment \
    -r 0.5.0 \
    -profile <container>[,<resources>] \
    --input samplesheet.csv \
    --outdir <OUTDIR>
  • --input: the samplesheet. See Samplesheet.
  • --outdir: the results directory. See Outputs.
  • -profile: see Profiles.
  • -r: the release to run. Always set it for real data.

Nextflow creates these in the launch directory:

work/        # task working directories (unless NXF_WORK or -work-dir is set)
<OUTDIR>/    # results
.nextflow/   # cache used by -resume
.nextflow.log

docs.title: Samplesheet
docs.text:
The samplesheet is a CSV or YAML file with one row per image. The minimum is a sample name, an image path and one step to run:

sample,run_backsub,run_cellpose,tiff,nuclear_channel,membrane_channels
slide1,true,true,/data/slide1.ome.tiff,DAPI,CD45:CD8
slide2,false,true,/data/slide2.ome.tiff,DAPI,CD45

Rules:

  • sample must be unique.
  • At most one of run_mesmer, run_cellpose and run_cellsam can be true in a row. To run two methods on one image, see Run several methods on one image.
  • A row must have at least one run_* column set to true. A row with only run_backsub set runs background subtraction and nothing else.
  • A row that runs a segmentation method needs nuclear_channel and membrane_channels.
  • Choose membrane channels that outline most cells. See Combining membrane channels.
  • Channel names are written without quotes. Separate membrane channels with :. Channel names can contain spaces but not ", ', : or ,.
  • Paths must not contain spaces.

The full column list is in Samplesheet. An example is in assets/samplesheet.csv.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Set parameters on the command line (--cellpose_diameter 40) or in a params file:

params.yaml
input: samplesheet.csv
outdir: results
cellpose_diameter: 40
generate_report: true

nextflow run WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment -r 0.5.0 -profile singularity -params-file params.yaml

Warning

Do not set parameters in a config file passed with -c. Use -c only for resources, executor settings and module arguments. See the nf-core configuration guide.

Every parameter is listed in Parameters. Run nextflow run WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment --help to list them in the terminal, and add --show_hidden to include hidden parameters.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Combine profiles with commas, for example -profile apptainer,medium. Later profiles override earlier ones.

  • Container profiles: apptainer, singularity, docker, podman, shifter, charliecloud. Use one of these. wave adds Seqera Wave containers and is used together with one of them. conda and mamba exist but are not supported.
  • Resource profiles for Slurm: small, medium, large, wehi_small, wehi_med, wehi_large. See Resource profiles.
  • Test profiles: see Test profiles.
  • debug: prints each task's host name and keeps work directories.

Without a container profile, every tool must be installed on your PATH. This is not supported.

The pipeline also loads institutional profiles from nf-core/configs at startup. Set NXF_OFFLINE=true to skip this when there is no internet access.

docs.title: Resuming a run
docs.text:
Add -resume to reuse the results of tasks that already finished with the same inputs and parameters:

nextflow run WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment -r 0.5.0 -profile singularity --input samplesheet.csv --outdir results -resume

To resume a specific earlier run, give its name: -resume <run-name>. nextflow log lists run names.

-resume restarts a failed task from the beginning. For a cell measurement task on a very large image, see Resume a killed measurement task.

docs.title: Caches on a cluster
docs.text:
The pipeline downloads data that is neither input nor output:

  • container images: tens of GB in total
  • Cellpose weights: about 1.2 GB
  • CellSAM and DeepCell weights: about 1.7 GB

By default all of this goes to your home directory. On a cluster with a home quota, a full home directory makes image pulls fail with:

FATAL: ... write /home/.../.apptainer/cache/oci-tmp/...: disk quota exceeded

Put every cache on scratch:

SCRATCH=/path/to/scratch/$USER

export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR=$SCRATCH/apptainer_cache
export SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR=$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR
mkdir -p "$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR"

nextflow run WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment \
    -profile apptainer,medium \
    -work-dir $SCRATCH/nextflow/work \
    --container_cache_dir $SCRATCH/apptainer_images \
    --cellpose_models_dir $SCRATCH/cellpose_models \
    --deepcell_cache_dir $SCRATCH/deepcell \
    --input samplesheet.csv \
    --outdir results
Cache Set with Holds Apptainer OCI layers (largest) APPTAINER_CACHEDIR env var Image layers unpacked while converting to SIF Converted container images --container_cache_dir The .img files Nextflow reuses across runs Cellpose weights --cellpose_models_dir Pre-downloaded Cellpose models DeepCell and CellSAM weights --deepcell_cache_dir <dir>/<username>/.deepcell/models/

Notes:

  • APPTAINER_CACHEDIR must be exported in the shell that starts Nextflow. Nextflow pulls images itself, not inside a task, so a config file cannot set it.
  • If --container_cache_dir is set and APPTAINER_CACHEDIR is unset or under $HOME, the pipeline stops at startup with an error that shows the commands to run.
  • With Apptainer or Singularity and the layer cache under $HOME, the pipeline prints a warning at startup.
  • The pipeline creates --deepcell_cache_dir if it does not exist and mounts it into the Mesmer and CellSAM containers.

docs.title: Cellpose model weights
docs.text:
Without --cellpose_models_dir, the pipeline downloads the Cellpose model once per run and gives the same copy to every patch task.

If compute nodes have no internet access, download the model once on a login node, in a Python environment with cellpose 4.2.1.1 installed:

CELLPOSE_LOCAL_MODELS_PATH=/path/to/scratch/cellpose_models \
    python -c "from cellpose import models; models.CellposeModel(gpu=False, pretrained_model='cpsam_v2')"

Then run with --cellpose_models_dir /path/to/scratch/cellpose_models.

  • Name the model you will run (cpsam_v2 above).
  • The directory must exist. The pipeline checks this at startup.
  • The directory must not be under /opt. The pipeline rejects this at startup, because mounting the host /opt hides the container's software.
  • cellpose.org serves the current weights for each model name. For results that can be repeated exactly, keep using the same --cellpose_models_dir.

docs.title: Changing resources
docs.text:
Each process has a label (process_low, process_medium, process_high, process_multi, process_single, process_gpu) that sets its CPUs, memory and time. The resource profiles set these per label. See Resource profiles.

To change one process, write a config file and pass it with -c:

custom.config
process {
    withName: 'CELLMEASUREMENT' {
        cpus   = 32
        memory = 400.GB
        time   = 72.h
    }
}

A task that fails with an exit code from 130 to 145, or 104, is retried once with twice the memory. Other failures stop the pipeline after running tasks finish.

See the nf-core guides on tuning resources and tool arguments.

docs.title: Running in the background
docs.text:
The Nextflow process must keep running until the pipeline finishes. Use one of:

  • a Slurm job (see Running at WEHI)
  • nextflow run ... -bg, which detaches from the terminal and writes to .nextflow.log
  • screen or tmux

To limit the memory of the Nextflow process itself, set:

export NXF_OPTS='-Xms1g -Xmx4g'

docs.title: Updating the pipeline
docs.text:
Nextflow caches the pipeline code after the first run and keeps using that copy. To update the cached copy:

nextflow pull WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment

With -r, Nextflow uses the named release regardless of the cached default branch.

docs.title: Running at WEHI
docs.text: This page covers Milton (the WEHI HPC) and the Seqera Platform.

docs.title: Load Nextflow
docs.text:
module load nextflow/25.10.0

Name the version. The default nextflow module is 23.10.0, which is older than the 24.04.2 the pipeline requires. The module also loads Apptainer and sets:

Variable Value NXF_WORK /vast/scratch/users/$USER/nextflow/work NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR /vast/scratch/users/$USER/nextflow/singularity_cache

So the work directory and the converted container images are already on scratch.

docs.title: Move the remaining caches off your home directory
docs.text:
The pipeline downloads tens of GB of container images and about 3 GB of model weights. Your home directory has a quota. Put every cache on scratch:

export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR=/vast/scratch/users/$USER/apptainer_cache
export SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR=$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR
mkdir -p "$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR"

and pass these parameters:

--cellpose_models_dir /vast/scratch/users/$USER/cellpose_models \
--deepcell_cache_dir /vast/scratch/users/$USER/deepcell

cellpose_models_dir must exist and contain the model before the run. See Cellpose model weights. If you leave it unset, the pipeline downloads the weights once per run instead.

APPTAINER_CACHEDIR must be exported in the shell that starts Nextflow. It cannot be set in a config file. See Caches on a cluster.

docs.title: Submit the run
docs.text:
Do not run Nextflow on a login node. Submit the Nextflow process as a Slurm job. It submits each pipeline task as its own Slurm job and must keep running until the pipeline finishes.

run_sp_segment.sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=sp_segment
#SBATCH --time=7-00:00:00
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=2
#SBATCH --mem=8G

module load nextflow/25.10.0
export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR=/vast/scratch/users/$USER/apptainer_cache
export SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR=$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR

nextflow run WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment \
    -r 0.5.0 \
    -profile apptainer,medium \
    --input samplesheet.csv \
    --outdir results \
    --deepcell_cache_dir /vast/scratch/users/$USER/deepcell \
    -resume

sbatch run_sp_segment.sh

Set --time longer than the whole run is expected to take, and within the partition's time limit. If the Nextflow job ends early, submit it again: -resume reuses every task that already finished.

The medium profile submits tasks to the regular partition and GPU tasks to gpuq with --gres=gpu:1 --constraint=Ampere. Choose the profile from the image size and cell density. See Resource profiles and Large and dense images.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Set your DeepCell token once. Nextflow stores it in ~/.nextflow/secrets:

nextflow secrets set DEEPCELL_ACCESS_TOKEN <your-token>

docs.title: KRONOS2 weights
docs.text: Download the KRONOS2 snapshot to a project or scratch directory, not under /opt. See KRONOS2 embeddings.

docs.title: Seqera Platform
docs.text: The pipeline is available on the Seqera Platform. The launch form is built from the pipeline's parameter schema, so each field has the same name and description as in Parameters. Parameters marked hidden (mask smoothing, Cellpose preprocessing) appear only when the form is set to show hidden parameters.

docs.title: Cellpose settings
docs.text:
This page explains the Cellpose defaults and the measurements behind them. For the parameter list, see Parameters.

All models the pipeline offers (cpsam_v2, cpsam, cpdino, cpdino-vitb) are Cellpose 4 transformer models. The defaults are the values the Cellpose authors use at test time. For most data, choose a model and change nothing else.

docs.title: What each setting does
docs.text: Parameter Default Change it? cellpose_pretrained_model cpsam_v2 Yes. This is the main choice. See Choose a segmentation method. cellpose_diameter 30 Only if cells are outside 7.5-120 pixels. cellpose_flow_threshold 0.4 Only if masks are visibly missing or ragged. cellpose_cellprob_threshold 0.0 Only if faint cells are missed or background is segmented. cellpose_min_area 100 Set it for your cell type and pixel size. See Minimum cell area. cellpose_gaussian_sigma 0 No. See Preprocessing. cellpose_clip_limit 0 No. See Preprocessing. cellpose_clahe_kernel_size not set No effect while cellpose_clip_limit is 0. cellpose_tile_norm_blocksize 0 No. See Tile-local normalisation. patch_width_pixel 3000 Only for memory or throughput. See Patch size.

docs.title: Diameter
docs.text:
Cellpose resizes the image by 30 / cellpose_diameter before segmentation and resizes the masks back afterwards. The default of 30 means no resizing.

Cellpose-SAM was trained on images resized between 0.25 and 4 times around a mean cell diameter of 30 pixels, so it handles cells from about 7.5 to 120 pixels without a diameter setting. Set the real diameter only for cells outside that range. A larger value, for example 90, shrinks the image 3 times and makes the run faster, but small objects are resolved less well.

Cellpose 4 has no automatic diameter estimate. A diameter of 0 means "do not resize", not "estimate". (The QuPath Cellpose extension's .diameter(0.0) estimate comes from Cellpose 2 and 3.)

The diameter does not remove any cells. Use cellpose_min_area for that.

docs.title: Flow threshold
docs.text:
Cellpose recomputes the flows that each finished mask implies and compares them with the flows the network predicted. Masks with a mean squared error above cellpose_flow_threshold are removed. This filter acts on shape only.

  • Raise it (0.6, 0.8) if visible cells are missing.
  • Lower it (0.2, 0.3) if you get ragged masks.
  • 0 turns the check off.

docs.title: Cell probability threshold
docs.text:
Pixels with a cell probability above cellpose_cellprob_threshold are used to build cells. This changes which cells are found and where each boundary falls, so it changes cell areas and every per-cell intensity measured over them.

The value is a logit, not a probability between 0 and 1. The useful range is about -6 to +6, and 0 is the midpoint.

  • Lower it (-1, -2) to find faint cells and make cells larger.
  • Raise it (1, 2) to stop segmenting dim background and make cells smaller.

docs.title: Model type
docs.text: cellpose_model_type no longer exists. Cellpose 4 ignores --model-type, so older runs that set cyto3 actually used cpsam. Setting it now stops the pipeline with an error. Use cellpose_pretrained_model.

docs.title: Preprocessing
docs.text:
Cellpose normalises each image by rescaling its 1st percentile to 0 and its 99th percentile to 1. It does nothing else: its sharpen_radius and smooth_radius default to 0, and it has no CLAHE step. The Cellpose-SAM paper states that its training images were normalised this way.

sopa, which runs Cellpose on each patch, adds two steps of its own before Cellpose:

Step Added by Setting in this pipeline gaussian filter (sopa default sigma = 1) sopa off: cellpose_gaussian_sigma = 0 CLAHE (sopa default clip_limit = 0.2) sopa off: cellpose_clip_limit = 0 rescale to 1st and 99th percentiles Cellpose on

To use sopa's steps, set --cellpose_clip_limit 0.2 --cellpose_gaussian_sigma 1.

docs.title: Why CLAHE is off
docs.text:
Every normalisation step is computed from the patch, so the input a cell gets depends on what else is in its patch. Patch overlap does not change this: overlap handles cells that cross a patch edge, not differences in normalisation.

CLAHE caused most of this dependence. Its kernel defaults to 1/8 of the patch size, so the contrast-enhancement scale changes with patch_width_pixel: at 0.28 µm/pixel, 52 µm for 1500-pixel patches, 105 µm for 3000 and 210 µm for 6000.

Cellpose-SAM was trained with random changes to global brightness and contrast, blur and noise, so it tolerates those. CLAHE is a local, position-dependent remapping, which was not part of its training.

Measured on the DAPI channel of a whole-slide COMET image: a 1024 × 1024 region was held fixed while the patch layout changed, and the change in the values Cellpose received for the same pixels was recorded (mean per-pixel spread, worst of patch size changed and patch origin shifted). A gaussian-only control measured 0.0000.

Nuclei per mm² DAPI-positive area sopa preprocessing Cellpose preprocessing 2,250 10.1% 0.1211 0.0265 2,932 14.6% 0.0651 0.0052 4,647 24.2% 0.0817 0.0075 12,006 66.2% 0.0758 0.0553

docs.title: Patch size
docs.text:
The same 1024 × 1024 region was segmented as part of a 1500-pixel patch and as part of a 3000-pixel patch, and the cells were matched by IoU. This measures how many cells keep the same outline when only patch_width_pixel changes:

Model sopa: IoU ≥ 0.90 Cellpose: IoU ≥ 0.90 sopa mean IoU Cellpose mean IoU cpsam_v2 103/267 (38.6%) 267/326 (81.9%) 0.869 0.928 cpsam 155/359 (43.2%) 271/323 (83.9%) 0.860 0.929 cpdino 74/201 (36.8%) 317/366 (86.6%) 0.855 0.936

With the default (Cellpose) preprocessing, patch_width_pixel mainly changes the number and length of tasks.

docs.title: Effect on results
docs.text:
Turning sopa's preprocessing off changes results. On dense patches:

Model Cell count Median cell area cpsam_v2 +8% to +35% −23% to −43% cpsam −3% to −10% −25% to −37% cpdino +28% to +54% −25% to −42%

Median cell area falls for every model, so per-cell intensities change. Do not pool results from pipeline versions before 0.5.0 with later results in one analysis.

The cells are now about 24-27 pixels in equivalent diameter against the configured 30. This is inside the range Cellpose-SAM was trained on, so cellpose_diameter does not need changing.

CLAHE also stretches an all-zero patch to the full intensity range, which skips Cellpose's check for empty patches (a 1st-99th percentile range below 0.001). On a test image, 13 of 84 patches at patch_width_pixel = 3000 were all zero. cpsam found 0 cells in such patches with and without CLAHE, so this cost time but did not create cells.

docs.title: Visual check
docs.text:
The defaults were run on a COMET image region (1683 × 2349 pixels at 0.28 µm/pixel, DAPI plus four membrane markers combined with max) and inspected in QuPath:

Method Cells Median area Median equivalent diameter Cellpose cpsam_v2 1,742 864 pixels² (68 µm²) 33.2 pixels (9.3 µm) Cellpose cpdino 1,751 916 pixels² (72 µm²) 34.2 pixels (9.6 µm) CellSAM 1,648 1,129 pixels² (89 µm²) 37.9 pixels (10.6 µm)

The three methods agree within 6% on cell count. CellSAM draws larger outlines around membrane signal.

docs.title: Limits of these measurements
docs.text:
• They measure reproducibility, not accuracy. No result was scored against annotations.
  • The normalisation measurements used the DAPI channel only. Whole-cell segmentation uses membrane channels, which are dimmer, and was not measured. CLAHE may help dim membrane channels. If your panel has weak membrane markers, compare both settings on your data.
  • CellSAM also applies CLAHE to each block, but its model was trained with CLAHE and uses a fixed 128-pixel kernel. Cellpose was not trained with CLAHE.

docs.title: Tile-local normalisation
docs.text:
cellpose_tile_norm_blocksize makes Cellpose compute the 1st and 99th percentiles per block inside the patch instead of once per patch. The default, 0, is Cellpose's own default (whole patch).

If you set it, use a block much larger than a cell. At 0.28 µm/pixel with a 30-pixel diameter, 512 pixels is 143 µm (about 17 nuclei across). 128 pixels is 36 µm (about 4 nuclei), and a block that size in sparse tissue can contain no nuclei. In testing at 128 pixels, the smallest per-block percentile range was 5.0 against 1670 for the whole patch, noise was stretched to the full range, and patch dependence became 3 to 24 times worse. Using it together with CLAHE also made results worse.

docs.title: GPU
docs.text: Cellpose runs on a GPU (SOPA_SEGMENTATIONCELLPOSE has the process_gpu label). On a machine without a GPU, override that label's settings in a -c config file. Cellpose then runs on CPU, more slowly.

docs.title: KRONOS2 marker handling
docs.text: This page explains how the pipeline prepares cells for KRONOS2. For how to run it, see KRONOS2 embeddings.

docs.title: Which cells
docs.text: The cells come from the cell measurement GeoJSON. Embedding row i is computed for GeoJSON feature i, so embeddings are joined to cells by position, not by spatial matching.

docs.title: Patch content
docs.text:
For each cell, the pipeline cuts a square patch of kronos_patch_size pixels (default 64) centred on the cell's centroid, from every channel KRONOS2 reads.

With kronos_isolate_cell = true (the default), pixels outside the cell outline are set to 0, so the embedding describes that cell and not its neighbours. A 64-pixel patch at 0.28 µm/pixel covers about 18 µm. Set it to false to keep the surrounding pixels.

docs.title: Intensity scaling
docs.text:
Pixel values are divided by a number derived from the image data type, as KRONOS2 does itself:

Image data type Divisor uint8 255 uint16 65535 float 400

Set kronos_max_value to use a different divisor.

docs.title: Marker names and normalisation
docs.text:
KRONOS2 normalises each channel with statistics stored for each marker in its 288-name vocabulary. It finds a channel's statistics by matching the channel name to the vocabulary exactly, ignoring separators. It has no alias or fuzzy matching.

A channel that does not match gets default statistics. KRONOS2 does not report this, and the result for that channel is less reliable. The pipeline therefore checks every name against the vocabulary first, using KRONOS2's own matching code, and fails the run when a name does not match. You then:

  • map the name to a vocabulary name with kronos_marker_mapping
  • leave the channel out with kronos_exclude_markers
  • or accept default statistics with kronos_allow_novel_defaults

The marker report lists the outcome for every channel.

docs.title: DAPI
docs.text: KRONOS2's only alias is for the nuclear stain: the channel passed as its preferred_dapi gets DAPI statistics whatever its name. The pipeline passes the samplesheet nuclear_channel, or kronos_nuclear_marker if set. A DRAQ5 or Hoechst channel therefore needs no mapping.

docs.title: Excluded channels
docs.text:
kronos_exclude_markers stops KRONOS2 reading a channel. The pipeline opens only the remaining channels. KRONOS2 uses all channels it reads together, so the set of channels affects every cell's embedding. Embeddings made with different channel sets cannot be compared.

remove_markers is different: it removes channels from the background-subtracted image, so no later step sees them.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: KRONOS2 runs in 32-bit floating point. The GPU library chooses calculation methods by batch size, so embeddings change very slightly (about 1e-4) with kronos_batch_size. The default, 16, reproduces the published values.

docs.title: Combining membrane channels
docs.text: When membrane_channels lists more than one channel, the pipeline combines them into one membrane channel before segmentation. This page describes how, and what was found when the two methods were compared.

docs.title: What the pipeline does
docs.text:
combine_method sets how the channels are combined:

  • max (default): the per-pixel maximum of the raw intensities.
  • norm_mean: each channel is rescaled so its 50th percentile is 0 and its 99.5th percentile is 1 (values below 0 are set to 0), then the per-pixel mean is taken and mapped linearly so its maximum is 65535.

COMBINECHANNELS does the combination, and Cellpose and CellSAM receive the combined channel. Mesmer combines the channels inside mesmer-segment, which has only max. A sample that runs Mesmer with norm_mean and more than one membrane channel stops the run at startup.

Each segmenter then rescales the channel it receives. Cellpose rescales to the 1st and 99th percentiles; Mesmer and CellSAM also apply contrast enhancement (CLAHE). This rescaling happens after the combination.

docs.title: Why there are two methods
docs.text:
Channels have different intensity ranges, set by exposure time, antibody and dilution. In a raw maximum, the channel with the highest values wins most pixels. A dim marker can lose everywhere, including in the cells it marks, so the segmenter may not see the membrane of cells marked only by that marker.

norm_mean puts every channel on the same scale before combining, so a dim marker is not hidden by a bright one. It also lowers the contrast of the brightest markers, and where several dim markers overlap it can turn their signal into an even haze with no edges between cells.

docs.title: What was found
docs.text:
max, norm_mean, the maximum of the rescaled channels and a single marker were compared with Cellpose, Mesmer and CellSAM on multiplexed tissue images, scored against manually labelled cell centroids and against outlines built from each labelled cell's own marker and nucleus.

  • No method was better than max for all three segmenters. With Cellpose, max found the most labelled cells.
  • With Cellpose, norm_mean gave about half as many objects without a nucleus as max. Most of those objects were small, bright membrane specks and fragments of fibres.
  • With Cellpose, norm_mean missed nucleated cells in dense regions where several dim markers overlap.
  • The method did not change the cell outlines. With every method, Cellpose outlines lay inside the marker-based outlines and were close to nucleus-sized.

So max stays the default. Use norm_mean when max outlines non-cell objects created by a bright marker, and check dense regions for missed cells.

Limitations: the outlines used for scoring were built from marker signal, not drawn by hand, and the comparison covered a small number of images.

docs.title: Choosing membrane channels
docs.text:
• A membrane marker present on most cells, such as Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase, β-catenin or HLA class I, outlines more cells than a mix of cell-type markers.
  • Each extra channel in a maximum can only raise the background. List the channels that outline cells, not every marker in the panel.
  • Check the combined image in combinechannels/<sample>_combined_channels.tiff before running a cohort. With max, if one marker dominates it, the other listed markers contribute little.

docs.title: Minimum cell area
docs.text:
Cellpose and CellSAM remove cells smaller than a minimum area. The defaults differ: 100 pixels² for Cellpose and 200 pixels² for CellSAM. To filter both methods the same way, set both parameters to the same value.

Parameter Default Measures Applied cellpose_min_area 100 pixels² area of the cell polygon, after smoothing by sopa, on each patch during segmentation cellsam_min_area 200 pixels² number of pixels in the cell's label once, after the tiles are merged
  • Both keep cells whose area is greater than or equal to the threshold.
  • 0 keeps every cell.
  • The unit is pixels², not µm², so the value does not follow pixel_size_microns. At 0.28 µm/pixel (COMET), 100 pixels² is 7.8 µm², about a 3.2 µm diameter disc, and 200 pixels² is 15.7 µm², about a 4.5 µm diameter disc. For another pixel size, recalculate the value.

docs.title: Polygon area against pixel count
docs.text:
The two filters measure area differently. On round and ragged test cells, the polygon area was 0.93 to 1.00 times the pixel count (median 0.99). So 200 on the CellSAM side is about the same as 202 on the Cellpose side.

Cellpose applies the filter per patch. This does not remove cells cut by a patch edge: patches overlap by patch_overlap_pixel, so a cut cell is whole in the neighbouring patch, and the whole copy is the one kept.

docs.title: Mesmer
docs.text: mesmer_min_nuclei_area (default 40 pixels²) is a separate filter. It removes small nuclei, not cells, and is applied inside the Mesmer tool.

docs.title: Tiling and straight cell edges
docs.text: Some cell outlines have straight horizontal or vertical edges that do not follow the image. This page describes where they come from, which ones are caused by tiling, and what was found when fixes were tested.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Source Segmenter Caused by tiling Effect CellSAM block stitching CellSAM Yes some cells are cut or halved at block seams sopa patch stitching Cellpose Yes straight edges on patch edges were rare in testing The Cellpose-SAM network output Cellpose No straight edges appear with or without patches Image border all No cells cut by the edge of the image

A straight edge here is a part of a cell boundary at least 15 pixels long that is exactly horizontal or exactly vertical. Natural cell boundaries are rarely aligned with the pixel grid over that length. Edges on the image border are not counted.

docs.title: CellSAM block seams
docs.text:
CellSAM (cellsam_use_wsi = true) segments the image in blocks of cellsam_block_size (600) pixels with cellsam_overlap (250) pixels of padding on each side. It then joins cells across a seam when the two blocks' versions overlap with an IoU of at least cellsam_iou_threshold (0.5), and trims every block back to its 600 × 600 core. Each cell that crosses a seam is therefore made from two predictions, one per side. This gives three faults:

  • The two predictions are joined but differ in shape, so the outline steps at the seam.
  • The two predictions overlap with an IoU below 0.5, so the cell stays as two cells split along the seam.
  • One block did not detect the cell, so only half of it is kept.

In testing, straight boundaries between CellSAM cells often lay on the 600 px block grid. Cellpose masks of the same images had none on that grid.

docs.title: Cellpose patches (sopa)
docs.text:
The Cellpose path segments patch_width_pixel (3000) pixel patches with patch_overlap_pixel (250) pixels of overlap. Each patch is normalised to its own 1st and 99th percentiles. sopa then merges two overlapping cells from different patches into their union when the overlap is at least half the area of the smaller cell (solve_conflicts, threshold 0.5), and otherwise keeps both.

Because each patch is normalised on its own, two neighbouring patches can see the same cells at different contrast, and their outlines of a cell in the shared strip can differ.

Normalisations and stitching rules compared:

  • Normalisation per patch (the current behaviour), or with the 1st and 99th percentiles of each channel over the whole region passed to Cellpose as fixed values (global).
  • Stitching by sopa (the current behaviour); keeping one version per cell, chosen by context (a version that does not touch a patch edge, then the one furthest from its patch edge); keeping one version per cell, chosen by mean cell probability; or centre ownership (a patch keeps the cells whose centre lies in its core).
  • One run of the whole region in a single Cellpose call, without patches.

Findings:

  • Global normalisation made the two patches' outlines agree more often but found fewer labelled cells away from seams. Buglakova et al. (2025) describe the same trade-off.
  • Segmenting the whole region in one call scored lowest.
  • Straight edges on patch edges were at about the level expected by chance for every method.
  • Keeping one version per cell, chosen by context, scored the same as sopa and left no overlapping outlines. Choosing by cell probability or by centre ownership scored lower; centre ownership loses cells whose two versions have their centres on opposite sides of the midline.

docs.title: Straight edges from Cellpose itself
docs.text:
Cellpose produces straight edges even when it runs on a whole image without patches, at the same places as in the pipeline.

Changes tested, with Cellpose run directly on the image:

Change Effect on straight edges niter 1000 or 2000 none Flip augmentation (augment) none tile_overlap 0.5 (default 0.1) none Watershed instead of the seed box none (identical masks) Image rotated 45° and rotated back most removed
  • The straight edges do not lie on Cellpose's internal 256 px tiles or on the 8 or 16 px patches of the network.
  • On a rotated image, Cellpose makes about as many straight edges along its own pixel axes, in different places. The straight edges follow the pixel grid that Cellpose runs on, not the tissue.
  • The straight edges are already in the cell probability map, so they come from the network output, not from mask construction.
  • Averaging the flows and cell probability of the 0° and 45° runs before building masks did not remove them, because the straight edges of the 0° map remain in the average.

Taking whole cells from a second run at 45° does remove most of them. Where a cell from the default run has a straight edge, and the 45° run has a matching cell (IoU ≥ 0.5) without one, the 45° cell replaces it. Cell counts, median areas and labelled cells found did not change. The rotated image is padded so that no tissue is cut, so the second run takes about twice the Cellpose GPU time of the first. This is not part of the pipeline.

docs.title: Not tested or not done
docs.text:
• The straight-edge measure does not separate wrong straight edges from correct ones (for example, the flat contact between two pressed nuclei).
  • No hand-drawn outlines were available, so outline accuracy was not measured.
  • None of the fixes on this page is in the pipeline. It uses sopa stitching, per-patch normalisation and a single Cellpose run.

docs.title: Related work
docs.text:
• Buglakova et al. (2025), Tiling artifacts and trade-offs of feature normalization in the segmentation of large biological images, arXiv:2503.19545.
  • Squidpy calculate_tiling_qc and assign_stitch_groups (experimental) flag cells with long straight, axis-aligned edges and group pieces cut at tile seams.
  • StarDist predict_instances_big discards a context margin from each block before stitching.

Note

Cellpose's model.eval normalises its input array in place. Pass a copy when calling it more than once on the same array or on overlapping views of one array.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: sp_segment follows the nf-core template (version 3.3.2). This page maps the code.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Path Contents main.nf Entry point. Runs initialisation, SP_SEGMENT, completion. workflows/sp_segment.nf The main workflow. Splits samples by method and step. subworkflows/local/ One subworkflow per segmentation path, plus utilities. modules/local/ Pipeline processes. modules/nf-core/backsub/ Background subtraction module from nf-core/modules. bin/ Python scripts called by the modules. conf/base.config Default resources per label. conf/modules.config Tool arguments (ext.args), publishing, GPU options. conf/test*.config Test profiles. nextflow.config Parameters, container and resource profiles. nextflow_schema.json Parameter schema. Drives validation, --help, Seqera and the docs. assets/schema_input.json Samplesheet schema. tests/ Test samplesheets, synthetic data, pytest tests.

docs.title: Startup checks
docs.text:
PIPELINE_INITIALISATION (subworkflows/local/utils_nfcore_sp_segment_pipeline/main.nf) runs before any task. It validates parameters against the schema, reads the samplesheet, and stops with an error for:

  • an unknown Cellpose model name or a missing custom model path
  • a missing cellpose_models_dir, or one under /opt
  • cellpose_model_type being set
  • container_cache_dir set while the Apptainer layer cache is under $HOME

docs.title: Main workflow
docs.text:
SP_SEGMENT reads each samplesheet row and sends it to one path:

Row Subworkflow run_backsub only BACKGROUNDSUBTRACT Mesmer, with background subtraction MESMER_SEGMENT_WBACKSUB Mesmer MESMER_SEGMENT Cellpose, with background subtraction SOPA_SEGMENT_WBACKSUB Cellpose SOPA_SEGMENT CellSAM, with background subtraction CELLSAM_SEGMENT_WBACKSUB CellSAM CELLSAM_SEGMENT

Each *_WBACKSUB subworkflow runs BACKGROUNDSUBTRACT and passes the background-subtracted image to the matching segmentation subworkflow.

Two steps run once at the top level instead of inside each path:

  • CELLPOSEMODEL downloads the Cellpose weights once per run. Every Cellpose patch task receives the same copy. It is skipped when cellpose_models_dir is set or cellpose_pretrained_model is a file.
  • KRONOS2EMBEDDINGS runs on the cell measurement output of every path.

docs.title: Segmentation subworkflows
docs.text:
All three run COMBINECHANNELS first. It writes a two-channel image: the nuclear channel and the membrane channels combined into one.

  • SOPA_SEGMENT runs SOPA_SEGMENT_COMPARTMENT for the whole-cell mask, and for the nuclear mask when use_whole_cell_only = false. Each run does SOPA_CONVERT (image to SpatialData zarr), SOPA_PATCHIFYIMAGE, SOPA_CELLPOSE (one SOPA_SEGMENTATIONCELLPOSE task per patch, then SOPA_RESOLVECELLPOSE) and PARQUETTOTIFF.
  • MESMER_SEGMENT runs MESMERSEGMENT as MESMERWC and MESMERNUC.
  • CELLSAM_SEGMENT runs CELLSAMSEGMENT as CELLSAMWC and CELLSAMNUC.

Each then runs SMOOTHMASKS (when smooth_masks = true), CELLMEASUREMENT and SEGMENTATIONREPORT (when generate_report = true).

docs.title: Modules and scripts
docs.text:
Module Script or tool Container EXTRACTMARKERS bin/extract_markers.py community.wave.seqera.io/library/tifffile_pandas_typer BACKSUB Background_subtraction (Schapiro lab) ghcr.io/schapirolabor/background_subtraction:v0.4.1 COMBINECHANNELS bin/combine_channels.py community.wave.seqera.io/library/tifffile_xarray_numpy_typer SOPA_*, CELLPOSEMODEL sopa 2.2.6 and cellpose 4.2.1.1 community.wave.seqera.io/library/python_pip_sopacellpose_cellpose PARQUETTOTIFF bin/parquet_to_tiff.py community.wave.seqera.io/library/tifffile_pyarrow_rasterio_shapely_pruned MESMERSEGMENT MesmerSegmentation CLI ghcr.io/wehi-soda-hub/mesmersegmentation:0.3.1 CELLSAMSEGMENT bin/cellsam_segment.py community.wave.seqera.io/library/python_tifffile_scikit-image_scikit-learn_pruned SMOOTHMASKS bin/smooth_masks.py community.wave.seqera.io/library/python_tifffile_numpy_scipy_pruned CELLMEASUREMENT cellmeasurement-py ghcr.io/wehi-soda-hub/cellmeasurement-py:0.2.2 KRONOS2EMBEDDINGS bin/kronos2_embeddings.py, bin/kronos2_common.py community.wave.seqera.io/library/kronos2embeddings SEGMENTATIONREPORT Quarto template with spatialVis ghcr.io/wehi-soda-hub/spatialvis:0.2.0

The Wave images are pinned by tag. The exact image for each process is in its main.nf.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: conf/modules.config publishes every process's outputs to <outdir>/<name>/, where <name> is the last part of the process name before any _, in lower case (for example SOPA_CONVERT to sopa/, MESMERWC to mesmerwc/). CELLPOSEMODEL is not published. KRONOS2EMBEDDINGS writes its GeoJSON to cellmeasurement/ and its report to kronos2embeddings/.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Check the issues for existing work on your idea. If there is none, open an issue.
  2. Fork the repository, or create a branch if you have write access.
  3. Branch from dev.
  4. Make the change, add or update tests, and update the docs (see Documentation).
  5. Add an entry under ## Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md.
  6. Open a pull request against dev. main is for releases only.

Pull requests are reviewed after the CI checks pass.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Follow the nf-core guidelines for processes, channels and configuration.
  • A new parameter needs a default in the params block of nextflow.config, an entry in nextflow_schema.json with the same default, a one-line description and, if needed, a longer help_text. Then regenerate the parameter reference with python3 docs/scripts/generate_reference.py.
  • A new samplesheet column needs an entry in assets/schema_input.json with a description, and a regenerated samplesheet reference.
  • Give each process a resource label from conf/base.config (process_low, process_medium, process_high, process_multi, process_single, process_gpu) and add tool arguments in conf/modules.config as ext.args.
  • Each process writes a versions.yml with the version of every tool it uses. Read versions from the tool, not from a hard-coded string.
  • Python scripts in bin/ need unit tests in tests/python/.

docs.title: Checks to run before a pull request
docs.text:
pre-commit run --all-files                       # prettier and editorconfig
pytest tests/python -q                           # bin/ script unit tests
python3 docs/scripts/generate_reference.py --check
mkdocs build --strict                            # needs docs/requirements.txt
nextflow run . -profile test,singularity --outdir results

See Testing for nf-test.

docs.title: Code of conduct
docs.text: See CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: The documentation site is built with MkDocs and Material for MkDocs from the Markdown files in docs/. The page order is set in nav in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Build locally
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv-docs
.venv-docs/bin/pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
.venv-docs/bin/mkdocs serve        # preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
.venv-docs/bin/mkdocs build --strict

--strict fails the build on any warning, including broken links. CI uses it.

docs.title: Generated pages
docs.text:
The tables in docs/reference/parameters.md and docs/reference/samplesheet.md are generated from nextflow_schema.json and assets/schema_input.json. Only the text between the <!-- BEGIN GENERATED --> and <!-- END GENERATED --> markers is replaced.

After changing either schema, run:

python3 docs/scripts/generate_reference.py

CI runs it with --check and fails if the committed pages are out of date. Prettier is told to skip these two files (.prettierignore), so it does not reformat the generated tables.

docs.title: Writing style
docs.text:
• Use short sentences and literal language.
  • Give exact parameter names and default values.
  • Describe what the pipeline does now. Put history in CHANGELOG.md.
  • Put implementation detail in the Background or Developer pages, not in the how-to and reference pages.
  • Use GitHub-style callouts (> [!NOTE], > [!WARNING]). They render on GitHub and on the site.
  • Do not put code blocks inside numbered lists. Prettier and MkDocs indent list content differently.
  • Link between pages with relative .md links, so links work on GitHub and on the site. Link to files outside docs/ with a full GitHub URL.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
.github/workflows/docs.yml builds the site on every pull request and deploys it with mike to the gh-pages branch:

Event Deployed as push to dev version dev release published version <tag>, alias latest (default)

The site is served at https://wehi-soda-hub.github.io/sp_segment/.

Note

A repository admin must enable GitHub Pages once: Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source: Deploy from a branch, branch gh-pages, folder / (root). The branch is created by the first deployment.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
Releases are made from dev to main. Tags have no v prefix (for example 0.5.0).

  1. On a branch from dev, set the new version: nf-core pipelines bump-version <version>. This updates manifest.version in nextflow.config and the other version strings.
  2. In CHANGELOG.md, rename ## Unreleased to ## v<version> - <YYYY-MM-DD> and add a new empty ## Unreleased above it.
  3. Open a pull request to dev, then a pull request from dev to main. On pull requests to main, lint runs with --release.
  4. Before merging, run the test profiles affected by the release on a GPU node. See Testing.
  5. After merging, create a GitHub release from main with the tag <version> and the changelog section as the release notes.

Publishing the release:

  • runs CI on the release
  • deploys the documentation as version <version> with the alias latest (see Documentation)
  • creates a new version of the Zenodo record, if the Zenodo GitHub integration is enabled for the repository

The pipeline DOI cited in the README is 10.5281/zenodo.17103183.

docs.title: What CI runs
docs.text:
Workflow Job What it runs .github/workflows/ci.yml test nextflow run . -profile test,singularity on Nextflow 24.04.2 and the latest release .github/workflows/linting.yml pre-commit prettier and editorconfig-checker .github/workflows/linting.yml pytest pytest tests/python -q .github/workflows/linting.yml nf-core nf-core pipelines lint .github/workflows/docs.yml build generate_reference.py --check and mkdocs build --strict

The test profile runs Cellpose with background subtraction on one synthetic image. CI has no GPU, so Mesmer, CellSAM and KRONOS2 are not run in CI. Run their test profiles locally on a GPU node before merging a change that affects them. nf-test is not run in CI (see below).

docs.title: Pipeline test profiles
docs.text:
Run every profile affected by a change. See Test profiles for the list. From a clone:

nextflow run . -profile test,singularity --outdir results/test
nextflow run . -profile test_mesmer,singularity --outdir results/test_mesmer
nextflow run . -profile test_cellsam,singularity --outdir results/test_cellsam
KRONOS2_MODEL_DIR=/path/to/KRONOS2 nextflow run . -profile test_mesmer_kronos2,singularity --outdir results/kronos2

At WEHI, submit these with sbatch and add a resource profile, for example -profile test_cellsam,apptainer,small, so GPU tasks go to gpuq.

docs.title: Python unit tests
docs.text:
pip install pytest numpy pandas tifffile rasterio shapely pyarrow typer
pytest tests/python -q

tests/python/conftest.py adds bin/ to the import path.

docs.title: nf-test
docs.text:
Modules and subworkflows have nf-test tests (tests/main.nf.test) with committed snapshots (main.nf.test.snap). Run them with:

nf-test test --profile test,singularity
nf-test test subworkflows/local/sopa_segment_compartment --profile test,singularity

To avoid downloading the 1.2 GB Cellpose weights on every run, export CELLPOSE_MODELS_DIR with a pre-downloaded model directory. tests/nextflow.config passes it to cellpose_models_dir.

docs.title: Updating snapshots
docs.text:
A change to a process graph changes the versions output and invalidates the snapshot. Update it in two steps:

  1. nf-test test <path> --profile test,singularity --update-snapshot
  2. Run the same test again without --update-snapshot. It must pass.

The second run is the check: --update-snapshot always agrees with what it just wrote. Update GPU-dependent snapshots (CellSAM) on a GPU node.

docs.title: Known state
docs.text:
Last full run: 2026-10-14, nf-test 0.9.5, Nextflow 25.10.0, Apptainer, on a WEHI A30 GPU node, with a valid DEEPCELL_ACCESS_TOKEN secret. 38 tests, 37 pass. The one failure:

  • segmentationreport - basic functionality: the report HTML has a different md5 on each run. The HTML contains no render date or time, so the cause is not known. Its snapshot was not updated.

Notes:

  • Mesmer and CellSAM tests that run the model (mesmersegment, cellsamsegment, mesmer_segment, mesmer_segment_wbacksub, cellsam_segment, cellsam_segment_wbacksub) need a valid DEEPCELL_ACCESS_TOKEN Nextflow secret. With an expired token they fail with API token ... is not valid.
  • smoothmasks has no snapshot of its output masks, and sopa_cellpose has no test.
  • To update one test, pass its hash: nf-test test <file>@<hash>. Only one @<hash> per file is run per command.
  • CellSAM determinism on CPU is not known. process_gpu sets accelerator = 1, so Docker test runs that looked like CPU runs used the GPU. To test CPU, set env.CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES = '' and process { withLabel: process_gpu { accelerator = 0 } } in tests/nextflow.config (do not commit this), run cellsam_segment - tiff twice and compare the outputs.
  • The backsub container writes a new UUID into each OME-TIFF, so the backgroundsubtract test checks the file name, not its md5.

docs.title: Before adding nf-test to CI
docs.text:
• GitHub's ubuntu-latest runners have no GPU. The process_gpu processes are SOPA_SEGMENTATIONCELLPOSE, CELLSAMSEGMENT and KRONOS2EMBEDDINGS. Decide how they run before enabling tests that reach them.
  • .nf-core.yml lists .github/workflows/nf-test.yml under lint.files_exist, so lint expects it to be absent. Adding it also turns on the actions_nf_test lint check. Add it once the suite passes.
  • Cache the Cellpose model directory keyed on the sopa container tag, and set CELLPOSE_MODELS_DIR:
- name: Restore Cellpose model cache
  id: cellpose-cache
  uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
    path: ${{ env.CELLPOSE_MODELS_DIR }}
    key: cellpose-models-${{ env.CELLPOSE_CONTAINER }}

- name: Fetch Cellpose model weights
  if: steps.cellpose-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
  run: |
    mkdir -p "${CELLPOSE_MODELS_DIR}"
    docker run --rm -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
      -e CELLPOSE_LOCAL_MODELS_PATH=/models \
      -v "${CELLPOSE_MODELS_DIR}:/models" \
      "${CELLPOSE_CONTAINER}" \
      python -c "from cellpose import models; models.CellposeModel(gpu=False)"
  • CellSAM downloads its 1.7 GB weights in every task unless deepcell_cache_dir is set. One measured download took 41 minutes.

docs.title: Choose a segmentation method
docs.text: Choose the method per sample with the run_cellpose, run_mesmer or run_cellsam column of the samplesheet. Each row can use one method.

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text:
Cellpose Mesmer CellSAM Input OME-TIFF OME-TIFF or MIBI TIFF OME-TIFF or MIBI TIFF Hardware GPU CPU GPU How it runs sopa splits the image into patches; one GPU task per patch one task per mask one GPU task per mask, tiled inside the task Default model cpsam_v2 (Cellpose-SAM) Mesmer (DeepCell) CellSAM generalist Token none DEEPCELL_ACCESS_TOKEN required DEEPCELL_ACCESS_TOKEN optional Size filter cellpose_min_area (100 pixels²) mesmer_min_nuclei_area (40 pixels², nuclei) cellsam_min_area (200 pixels²) Edge cells kept removed (mesmer_remove_border_cells) removed (cellsam_remove_border_cells) Main parameters cellpose_pretrained_model, patch_width_pixel mesmer_maxima_threshold, mesmer_interior_threshold cellsam_bbox_threshold, cellsam_block_size

All three segment whole cells from the nuclear channel plus the combined membrane channels. With use_whole_cell_only = false, they also segment nuclei from the nuclear channel alone, and cell measurement matches each nucleus to a cell.

docs.title: Which to use
docs.text:
• Start with Cellpose for COMET and other OME-TIFF images. The defaults need no tuning. See Cellpose settings.
  • Use Mesmer or CellSAM for MIBI images, because Cellpose needs an OME-TIFF.
  • Use Mesmer if no GPU is available.
  • CellSAM draws larger cell boundaries around membrane signal than Cellpose. On one COMET test region, the median CellSAM cell area was about 30% larger than the Cellpose cpsam_v2 median.

Check results in QuPath before choosing for a whole cohort. To compare methods on the same image, see Run several methods on one image.

docs.title: Run time
docs.text:
• Cellpose runs one short GPU task per patch (patch_width_pixel, default 3000). Many patches can run at once if GPUs are free.
  • CellSAM runs one GPU task per mask for the whole image. On whole-slide COMET images this has taken from about 1 to 22 hours per image, depending on the number of cells.
  • Mesmer runs one CPU task per mask.

docs.title: Cellpose models
docs.text:
Set cellpose_pretrained_model:

Value Model cpsam_v2 Default. The current Cellpose-SAM model. cpsam The previous Cellpose-SAM model. Use it to match results from before cellpose 4.2. cpdino DINOv3 backbone (ViT-L, about 303 million parameters). cpdino-vitb Smaller DINOv3 backbone (ViT-B). a file path Your own trained Cellpose model. The file must exist.

On the 119-cell synthetic test image, compared with the earlier pipeline version (which used cpsam):

Model Cells Foreground IoU Cells matched at IoU ≥ 0.90 cpsam 119 0.9987 119 of 119 (100%) cpsam_v2 119 0.9552 112 of 119 (94%) cpdino 123 0.9251 106 of 119 (89%)

This shows the models differ. It does not show which is more accurate for your tissue.

docs.title: KRONOS2 embeddings
docs.text:
KRONOS2 is a foundation model for multiplex spatial proteomics. The pipeline uses it to add a 768-value embedding to every cell in the cell measurement GeoJSON. Embeddings can be used for clustering and other downstream analysis.

KRONOS2 runs after cell measurement, on the same image the cells were measured on (the background-subtracted image when run_backsub = true). It needs a GPU.

docs.title: Get the model
docs.text:
The weights are gated on Hugging Face. Request access to MahmoodLab/KRONOS2, then download the full snapshot:

hf auth login
hf download MahmoodLab/KRONOS2 --local-dir /path/to/KRONOS2 --exclude "demo_image/*"
  • Download the whole snapshot. The loader imports the dinov2 package that is part of the snapshot, so a partial download does not work.
  • Do not put the snapshot under /opt. The host /opt would be mounted over the container's /opt, and the task would fail with /usr/bin/env: 'python3': No such file or directory.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
nextflow run WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment \
    -profile apptainer,medium \
    --input samplesheet.csv \
    --outdir results \
    --enable_kronos true \
    --kronos_model_path /path/to/KRONOS2

Outputs:

  • cellmeasurement/<sample>.geojson.gz with kronos_emb_0 to kronos_emb_767 added to every cell.
  • kronos2embeddings/<sample>_marker_report.txt, which lists how each channel was matched.

See Outputs.

docs.title: Fix unmatched marker names
docs.text:
KRONOS2 has a vocabulary of 288 marker names. It matches a channel name to the vocabulary exactly, ignoring separators: CD-8, CD_8 and CD8 match each other. Spelling variants do not match: Cytokeritin does not match CYTOKERATIN.

If any channel name does not match, the run fails and lists the names. Read the marker report, then do one of the following for each name.

docs.title: The channel is a marker under a different name
docs.text:
Map it to the vocabulary name with a JSON file:

kronos_marker_mapping.json
{
  "Collagen 4": "COLLAGENiv",
