  "Cytokeritin": "CYTOKERATIN",
  "VISA": "VISTA"
}

--kronos_marker_mapping /path/to/kronos_marker_mapping.json

The value can also be inline JSON: --kronos_marker_mapping '{"VISA": "VISTA"}'. Keys that start with _ are ignored, so they can hold comments. A value that is neither an existing file nor valid JSON fails the run. Mapping keys that match no channel are listed in the marker report.

The mapping changes only the names given to KRONOS2. Channel names in the image and in the GeoJSON do not change. An example file is in docs/examples/kronos_marker_mapping.json.

docs.title: The channel is not a marker
docs.text:
For autofluorescence, blank or empty channels, stop KRONOS2 from reading the channel:

--kronos_exclude_markers 'Autofluorescence'
  • Separate several names with commas.
  • Names are case sensitive and must match the image's channel names, before any mapping.
  • A name that matches no channel fails the run.
  • The nuclear channel cannot be excluded.
  • Only KRONOS2 skips the channel. The image, segmentation and the channel's cell measurements are not changed.

With background subtraction, KRONOS2 reads the background-subtracted image, so channels in remove_markers are already gone. Do not list them in kronos_exclude_markers, or the run fails with "no such channel".

docs.title: Accept default statistics
docs.text: --kronos_allow_novel_defaults true lets the run continue. KRONOS2 then normalises each unmatched channel with default statistics instead of marker-specific ones, which makes that channel's contribution less reliable. Use mapping or exclusion where possible.

docs.title: Nuclear channel
docs.text: KRONOS2 treats one channel as its DAPI channel. The pipeline uses the samplesheet nuclear_channel for this, so slides stained with DRAQ5 or Hoechst get DAPI statistics. Set kronos_nuclear_marker to use a different channel.

docs.title: Keep embeddings comparable across a cohort
docs.text:
Use the same settings for every image you want to compare:

  • the same kronos_exclude_markers list. KRONOS2 uses all channels together, so excluding a channel changes every cell's embedding.
  • the same kronos_patch_size (default 64) and kronos_isolate_cell (default true).
  • the same kronos_batch_size (default 16). Embeddings change very slightly with batch size; 16 reproduces the published values.

Embeddings from KRONOS1 (pipeline versions before 0.5.0, 384 values per cell) cannot be compared with KRONOS2 embeddings.

For details of normalisation and patch content, see KRONOS2 marker handling.

docs.title: Large and dense images
docs.text: Whole-slide images can need hundreds of GB of memory and many hours per task. Memory use depends more on the number of cells than on the file size.

docs.title: Choose a resource profile
docs.text:
Image Profile up to 150 GB small up to 300 GB medium up to 600 GB large millions of cells (for example large tumour regions) wehi_med or wehi_large

The full requests are in Resource profiles. If a task fails for lack of memory, it is retried once with twice the memory. If it fails again, move to the next profile, or raise that one process with a -c config file. See Changing resources.

docs.title: Reduce memory
docs.text:
• List only the membrane channels you need in membrane_channels.
  • Keep gzip_geojson = true (the default). Uncompressed GeoJSON for a whole slide can exceed 100 GB.
  • Leave neighbors = 0 (the default) unless you need neighbourhood features.
  • For a quick look, set downsample_factor 2 (or higher) to measure on a downsampled image. Area and length measurements are scaled back to full resolution.
  • Set enable_measurements false to write cell outlines only.

docs.title: Speed up cell measurement
docs.text:
Cell measurement runs on tiles in parallel, one tile per CPU.

  • tile_size (default 2048): aim for 2 to 4 times more tiles than CPUs.
  • tile_overlap (default 200): at least the diameter of the largest cell.

Polygon extraction is the slowest part of cell measurement on images with millions of cells. If the task can hit its time limit, set geometry_checkpoint_dir. See Resume a killed measurement task.

docs.title: Cellpose patches
docs.text:
Cellpose runs on square patches of patch_width_pixel pixels (default 3000) that overlap by patch_overlap_pixel (default 250). Each patch is a separate GPU task.

  • Patch size changes the number of tasks, not the result: with the default preprocessing, about 82-87% of cells keep the same outline (IoU ≥ 0.90) when the patch width changes from 1500 to 3000 pixels. See Cellpose settings.
  • Larger patches give fewer, longer tasks. This helps when the GPU queue is busy, because each task waits in the queue.
  • Set patch_overlap_pixel to at least the diameter of the largest cell.

docs.title: QuPath cannot load the GeoJSON
docs.text: Cells with very complex outlines can make QuPath fail with StackOverflowError. Set --smooth_masks true to simplify the outlines before measurement. --smooth_method shapely reduces the number of vertices directly. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Run several methods on one image
docs.text:
Each samplesheet row runs at most one segmentation method, and each sample value must be unique. To run two or three methods on one image, add one row per method with a different sample name and the same tiff:

sample,run_backsub,run_mesmer,run_cellpose,run_cellsam,tiff,nuclear_channel,membrane_channels
slide1_cellpose,true,false,true,false,/data/slide1.ome.tiff,DAPI,CD45:Pan-Cytokeratin
slide1_mesmer,true,true,false,false,/data/slide1.ome.tiff,DAPI,CD45:Pan-Cytokeratin
slide1_cellsam,true,false,false,true,/data/slide1.ome.tiff,DAPI,CD45:Pan-Cytokeratin

Each row writes its own files, for example cellmeasurement/slide1_cellpose.geojson.gz and cellmeasurement/slide1_mesmer.geojson.gz.

Background subtraction runs once per row, so this example runs it three times. To run it once, run a first pass with run_backsub only, then use backsub/<sample>.ome.tif as the tiff for the segmentation rows with run_backsub = false.

The pipeline stops at startup if two rows share a sample value, or if a row sets more than one of run_mesmer, run_cellpose and run_cellsam.

docs.title: View results in QuPath
docs.text: The cell measurement GeoJSON can be opened in QuPath on top of the image it was made from.

docs.title: Which image to open
docs.text:
Open the image the cells were measured on:

  • with run_backsub = true: backsub/<sample>.ome.tif
  • otherwise: the tiff from the samplesheet

The cell coordinates are in pixels of that image.

docs.title: Import the cells
docs.text:
1. Open the image in a QuPath project.
  2. Drag cellmeasurement/<sample>.geojson.gz onto the image window, or use File > Import objects from file.
  3. Open Measure > Show detection measurements to see the measurements.

If QuPath does not accept the .geojson.gz file, decompress it first (gunzip -k <sample>.geojson.gz), or set --gzip_geojson false to write uncompressed files.

Measurement names are described in Outputs.

docs.title: Large GeoJSON files
docs.text: Whole-slide GeoJSON files can be several GB even when compressed, and can be too large to import through the QuPath interface. The separate import_large_geojson Nextflow pipeline imports large GeoJSON files into a QuPath project in batch.

docs.title: Errors on import
docs.text:
• StackOverflowError: some cell outlines have too many vertices. Re-run with --smooth_masks true, and use --smooth_method shapely if that is not enough. See Mask smoothing options.
  • The cells appear flipped relative to the image (Mesmer only): set --mesmer_transpose_mask true.

docs.title: Resume a killed measurement task
docs.text:
On whole-slide images with millions of cells, polygon extraction is the slowest part of CELLMEASUREMENT. If the task is killed by its time limit or by running out of memory, Nextflow's retry and -resume start it again from the beginning.

Set geometry_checkpoint_dir to save progress. The task then writes each completed batch of cells to that directory, and a retried or resumed task continues from the last completed batch.

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
nextflow run WEHI-SODA-Hub/sp_segment \
    -profile apptainer,medium \
    --input samplesheet.csv \
    --outdir results \
    --geometry_checkpoint_dir /vast/scratch/users/$USER/sp_segment_checkpoints \
    -resume
  • The directory must be outside the Nextflow work directory. Each retry runs in a new work directory, so a checkpoint inside the work directory is not found.
  • Each sample and each mask gets its own subdirectory.
  • geometry_batch_size (default 2000) sets the number of cells per batch. Smaller batches save progress more often but add overhead. A killed task loses at most one batch per worker.

docs.title: When checkpoints are not used
docs.text:
A checkpoint is ignored, and extraction starts again, if any of these differ from the run that wrote it:

  • polygon simplification settings
  • geometry_batch_size
  • mask dimensions
  • number of cells

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text: Checkpoints are not deleted automatically. Delete the directory after the run has finished successfully.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Set parameters on the command line with two dashes (--cellpose_diameter 40) or in a params file passed with -params-file. Do not set them in a -c config file.

Parameters marked hidden are left out of --help and the Seqera Platform launch form unless hidden parameters are shown (--show_hidden). They work the same as other parameters.

This page is generated from nextflow_schema.json.

docs.title: Input/output options
docs.text:
Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

Parameter Type Default Description input (required) string Path to the samplesheet (CSV or YAML) that lists the images to process. outdir (required) string The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure. email string Email address for completion summary.

docs.title: input
docs.text: One row per image. Required columns: sample and tiff. See the Samplesheet page of the documentation for every column.

docs.title: email
docs.text: The pipeline sends a summary e-mail to this address when the run finishes. You can set it in ~/.nextflow/config instead of on the command line.

docs.title: Background subtraction options
docs.text:
Parameters used for background subtraction.

Parameter Type Default Description remove_markers string TRITC,Cy5 Comma-separated channel names to remove from the background-subtracted image. Names are case sensitive.

docs.title: Combine options
docs.text:
Parameters used for combining membrane channels.

Parameter Type Default Description combine_method string: max, norm_mean max How to combine several membrane channels into one. max: the per-pixel maximum. norm_mean: the mean of the channels after rescaling each to its own 50th-99.5th percentile.

docs.title: combine_method
docs.text: Used when membrane_channels lists more than one channel. max is used by Mesmer, Cellpose and CellSAM. norm_mean is used by Cellpose and CellSAM only; a sample that runs Mesmer with norm_mean and more than one membrane channel stops the run at startup. With max, a dim marker is hidden wherever a brighter marker has signal; norm_mean puts every marker on the same scale. See Combining membrane channels.

docs.title: Cell processing options
docs.text:
Parameters used for cell processing.

Parameter Type Default Description use_whole_cell_only boolean true Use only the whole-cell segmentation to process cells (skip nuclear segmentation).

docs.title: use_whole_cell_only
docs.text: Defaults to true: only the whole-cell segmentation is used to process cells. Nuclei are not segmented and nuclear measurements are not produced; cell, erosion, and expansion measurements are kept. Set to false to also segment nuclei and measure them.

docs.title: SOPA options
docs.text:
Parameters used by SOPA for image patching.

Parameter Type Default Description technology string: ome_tif ome_tif Image type for the sopa conversion. Only ome_tif is supported. patch_width_pixel integer 3000 Width and height of each square patch, in pixels, for Cellpose segmentation. patch_overlap_pixel integer 250 Overlap between neighbouring patches, in pixels. Set it to at least the diameter of the largest cell.

docs.title: Cellpose options
docs.text:
Parameters used by Cellpose for the cell segmentation.

Parameter Type Default Description cellpose_diameter integer 30 Expected cell diameter in pixels. Cellpose resizes the image by 30 / diameter before segmentation. cellpose_min_area number 100 Discard cells smaller than this many square pixels. Higher keeps fewer cells; 0 keeps every mask. cellpose_flow_threshold number 0.4 Maximum flow error allowed for a mask to be kept. Higher finds more cells, including ill-shaped ones; lower keeps fewer, better-formed ones. cellpose_cellprob_threshold number 0.0 Cutoff on Cellpose's per-pixel cell probability. Lower finds more and larger cells; higher finds fewer and smaller ones. cellpose_model_type (hidden) string Retired. Cellpose 4 ignores --model-type; use cellpose_pretrained_model instead. cellpose_pretrained_model string cpsam_v2 Cellpose model to segment with: cpsam_v2 (default), cpsam, cpdino, cpdino-vitb, or a path to a custom model. cellpose_models_dir string Directory holding pre-staged Cellpose model weights. If set, the pipeline uses it instead of downloading them.

docs.title: cellpose_diameter
docs.text:
Cellpose-SAM models were trained on cell diameters from 7.5 to 120 pixels (mean 30), so the default of 30 suits most data and means no resizing.

  • Set the real diameter if your cells are outside 7.5-120 pixels.
  • A larger value (for example 90) shrinks the image and makes the run faster, but small objects are resolved less well.

This parameter does not remove any cells. Use cellpose_min_area to remove small objects. A value of 0 means no resizing; Cellpose 4 has no automatic diameter estimate.

docs.title: cellpose_min_area
docs.text:
Applied by sopa to each patch during segmentation. The unit is pixels², not µm², so it does not change with pixel_size_microns. At 0.28 µm/pixel (COMET), 100 pixels² is 7.8 µm², about a 3.2 µm diameter disc.

cellsam_min_area uses the same unit and defaults to 200. mesmer_min_nuclei_area is a separate filter on nuclei.

docs.title: cellpose_flow_threshold
docs.text:
Cellpose recomputes the flows each mask implies and compares them with the flows the network predicted. Masks with a mean squared error above this value are removed. This filter acts on shape only.

  • Raise it (0.6, 0.8) if visible cells are missing.
  • Lower it (0.2, 0.3) if you get ragged, ill-shaped masks.
  • 0 turns the check off.

The default 0.4 is Cellpose's default.

docs.title: cellpose_cellprob_threshold
docs.text:
Pixels above this value are used to build cells, so it changes which cells are found and where each cell boundary falls. A change here changes cell areas and therefore every per-cell intensity.

The value is not a probability between 0 and 1. It is a logit: the useful range is about -6 to +6, and 0 is the midpoint.

  • Lower it (-1, -2) to find faint cells and make cells larger.
  • Raise it (1, 2) to stop segmenting background and make cells smaller.

The default 0.0 is Cellpose's default.

docs.title: cellpose_model_type
docs.text: Cellpose >=4.0.1 logs model_type argument is not used in v4.0.1+. Ignoring this argument, and sopa only reads it on the cellpose<4 code path, so it never had any effect on a v4 run. Setting it now raises an error rather than being silently discarded.

docs.title: cellpose_pretrained_model
docs.text:
Built-in models (cellpose 4.2.1.1):

  • cpsam_v2: default; the current Cellpose-SAM model.
  • cpsam: the previous Cellpose-SAM model. Use it to reproduce results from before cellpose 4.2.
  • cpdino: DINOv3 backbone (ViT-L).
  • cpdino-vitb: smaller DINOv3 backbone (ViT-B).

Any other value is treated as a path to a custom model and must exist; the pipeline checks this at startup. Built-in models are downloaded once per run, or read from cellpose_models_dir if set. See CITATIONS.md for the DINOv3 licence terms.

docs.title: cellpose_models_dir
docs.text: A directory that holds the Cellpose model cache (for example a cpsam_v2 file). Use it when compute nodes have no internet access. The directory must exist and must not be under /opt.

docs.title: Cellpose preprocessing options
docs.text:
Intensity preprocessing applied before Cellpose segmentation.

The defaults make the pipeline match Cellpose's own preprocessing: rescale each patch to its 1st and 99th percentiles and nothing else. sopa's gaussian filter and CLAHE are turned off. To restore sopa's behaviour, set cellpose_clip_limit to 0.2 and cellpose_gaussian_sigma to 1. See the Cellpose preprocessing page of the documentation for the measurements behind these defaults.

Parameter Type Default Description cellpose_tile_norm_blocksize (hidden) integer 0 Block size in pixels for Cellpose's tile-local intensity normalisation. 0 uses Cellpose's whole-patch default. cellpose_clip_limit (hidden) number 0 sopa's CLAHE clip limit, applied before Cellpose. Defaults to 0 in this pipeline, disabling CLAHE; null restores sopa's default of 0.2. cellpose_clahe_kernel_size (hidden) integer Kernel size in pixels for sopa's CLAHE. Unset uses skimage's default of patch.shape // 8, which scales with patch_width_pixel. cellpose_gaussian_sigma (hidden) number 0 Sigma for sopa's gaussian smoothing, applied before Cellpose. Defaults to 0 in this pipeline, disabling it; null restores sopa's default of 1.

docs.title: cellpose_tile_norm_blocksize
docs.text:
When greater than 0, Cellpose computes the 1st/99th percentiles separately for each block of this size inside the patch instead of once for the whole patch.

Use a block much larger than a cell. At 0.28 µm/pixel, 512 pixels is 143 µm (about 17 nuclear diameters). Small blocks (for example 128 pixels) can contain no nuclei in sparse tissue; their noise is then stretched to the full intensity range and results get worse.

docs.title: cellpose_clip_limit
docs.text: sopa applies CLAHE (skimage.exposure.equalize_adapthist) to each patch before Cellpose. Cellpose itself has no CLAHE step and its models were not trained with it. 0 turns CLAHE off. With CLAHE on, results change with patch_width_pixel, because the CLAHE kernel size is derived from the patch size.

docs.title: cellpose_clahe_kernel_size
docs.text: If unset, skimage uses 1/8 of the patch height and width: 375 pixels at patch_width_pixel 3000. Setting a fixed value stops the kernel size changing with the patch size. Has no effect while cellpose_clip_limit is 0.

docs.title: cellpose_gaussian_sigma
docs.text: sopa applies a gaussian filter to each patch before Cellpose. Cellpose applies no smoothing by default. 0 turns the filter off. Raise it only if your images are noisy enough to need smoothing before segmentation.

docs.title: Mesmer options
docs.text:
Parameters used by the MesmerSegmentation tool.

Parameter Type Default Description mesmer_segmentation_level integer Segmentation level passed to Mesmer as --segmentation-level (legacy option). Unset by default. mesmer_maxima_threshold number 0.1 Mesmer maxima threshold. Lower values give more cells; higher values give fewer cells. mesmer_interior_threshold number 0.3 Mesmer interior threshold. Higher values give smaller nuclei and cells. mesmer_maxima_smooth number 0 Smoothing applied to Mesmer's maxima signal. Higher values give more regular shapes. mesmer_min_nuclei_area number 40 Minimum nucleus area in pixels². Smaller nuclei are removed by Mesmer. mesmer_remove_border_cells boolean true Remove cells that touch the image border. mesmer_pixel_expansion integer 3 Number of pixels to expand each Mesmer cell after segmentation. mesmer_padding integer 0 Number of pixels to crop from each side of the image before Mesmer segmentation. mesmer_transpose_mask boolean false Transpose the Mesmer output mask. Enable this only if the mask is flipped relative to the image.

docs.title: CellSAM options
docs.text:
Parameters used by CellSAM for foundation model cell segmentation.

Parameter Type Default Description cellsam_bbox_threshold number 0.4 Confidence threshold for CellSAM cell detections. Lower values (0.3-0.4) find more cells on images unlike the training data. cellsam_block_size integer 600 Tile size in pixels for whole-slide CellSAM processing. cellsam_overlap integer 250 Overlap between CellSAM tiles, in pixels. Set it to at least the typical cell diameter. cellsam_iou_depth integer 250 Distance in pixels searched for duplicate cells at tile boundaries. cellsam_iou_threshold number 0.5 IoU above which two overlapping cells at a tile boundary are merged. cellsam_use_wsi boolean true Process the image in tiles (whole-slide mode). Required for large images. cellsam_gauge_cell_size boolean false Run a first CellSAM pass to estimate cell size before segmentation. cellsam_low_contrast_enhancement boolean false Apply contrast enhancement before segmentation, for low-contrast images. cellsam_model_path string Path to custom CellSAM model weights. If unset, the CellSAM generalist model is used (v1.2 when DEEPCELL_ACCESS_TOKEN is set). cellsam_min_area integer 200 Remove cells smaller than this many pixels². 0 keeps every cell. cellsam_remove_border_cells boolean true Remove CellSAM cells that touch the image edge.

docs.title: cellsam_min_area
docs.text:
CellSAM counts each cell's pixels and applies the filter once, after the tiles are merged. The unit is pixels², not µm². At 0.28 µm/pixel, 200 pixels² is 15.7 µm². Cells with an area equal to the threshold are kept.

cellpose_min_area measures the area of the cell polygon instead. On test cells the polygon area was 0.93-1.00 times the pixel count (median 0.99), so at the same value the two filters remove almost the same cells. cellpose_min_area defaults to 100.

docs.title: cellsam_remove_border_cells
docs.text: Cells cut by the image edge are incomplete, so they are removed by default. Set to false to keep them.

docs.title: KRONOS2 embedding options
docs.text:
Options for KRONOS2 per-cell foundation-model embeddings

KRONOS2 is a foundation model for multiplex spatial proteomics. These parameters control the optional step that adds a 768-value embedding to every cell after cell measurement.

Parameter Type Default Description enable_kronos boolean false Enable KRONOS2 per-cell embedding extraction. kronos_model_path string Path to a full KRONOS2 snapshot directory, or a Hugging Face repo id. kronos_patch_size integer 64 Size of cell-centered patches to extract for KRONOS inference. kronos_batch_size integer 16 Batch size for inference. KRONOS2 runs fp32 and cuBLAS picks batch-dependent kernels, so this shifts embeddings slightly; 16 reproduces the published values. kronos_num_workers integer 4 Number of parallel DataLoader workers for loading and preprocessing cell patches. kronos_max_value number Override the intensity divisor. Unset derives it from the image dtype (uint8=255, uint16=65535, float=400), matching KRONOS2 itself. kronos_marker_mapping string JSON file, or an inline JSON object, that maps channel names to KRONOS2 marker names, e.g. {"Collagen 4": "COLLAGENiv"}. kronos_exclude_markers string Comma-separated channel names that KRONOS2 does not read, e.g. 'Autofluorescence'. Other steps still use these channels. kronos_nuclear_marker string Channel that KRONOS2 treats as its DAPI channel. Defaults to the samplesheet nuclear_channel. kronos_isolate_cell boolean true Zero pixels outside the target cell so each embedding describes that cell rather than its surrounding neighbourhood. kronos_allow_novel_defaults boolean false Continue when a channel name is not in the KRONOS2 vocabulary. That channel is normalised with default statistics. Off by default, so the run fails instead.

docs.title: enable_kronos
docs.text: Set to true to compute KRONOS2 embeddings after cell measurement. Requires kronos_model_path.

docs.title: kronos_model_path
docs.text:
Request access to MahmoodLab/KRONOS2 on Hugging Face, then download the full snapshot:

hf download MahmoodLab/KRONOS2 --local-dir /path/to/KRONOS2 --exclude "demo_image/*"

A partial download does not work, because the loader imports the dinov2 package bundled in the snapshot. Do not store the snapshot under /opt.

docs.title: kronos_patch_size
docs.text: Side length in pixels of the square patch centred on each cell. Larger patches include more surrounding tissue and take longer.

docs.title: kronos_batch_size
docs.text: Number of cell patches per GPU batch. Larger batches are faster and use more GPU memory. Embeddings change very slightly with batch size; 16 reproduces the published values.

docs.title: kronos_num_workers
docs.text: Number of CPU processes that read and prepare patches while the GPU runs. 0 reads in the main process. Set it to the number of CPUs allocated to the task.

docs.title: kronos_marker_mapping
docs.text:
KRONOS2 matches marker names exactly, ignoring separators (CD-8, CD_8 and CD8 match). There is no alias or fuzzy matching, so a spelling variant such as Cytokeritin does not match CYTOKERATIN. The run fails if any channel does not match, unless kronos_allow_novel_defaults is true.

The mapping changes only the names given to KRONOS2. Channel names in the image and the GeoJSON are not changed. A value that is neither an existing file nor valid JSON fails the run.

docs.title: kronos_exclude_markers
docs.text:
Use it for channels that are not markers: autofluorescence, blanks, empty cycles. The channel stays in the image and keeps its cell measurements.

  • Names are case sensitive and are matched against the image's channel names before kronos_marker_mapping is applied.
  • A name that matches no channel fails the run.
  • The nuclear channel cannot be excluded.
  • Excluding a channel changes every cell's embedding. Use the same list for every image in a cohort.

docs.title: Cell measurement options
docs.text:
Parameters used for cell measurement.

Parameters for the cell measurement step (cellmeasurement-py).

Parameter Type Default Description enable_measurements boolean true Enable cell measurement step. percentiles string 70,80,90,95,99 Comma-separated list of percentiles to calculate for each marker (e.g. 80,90,95,99). erosion_steps boolean true Measure intensity in 5 equal-area erosion bins working inward from the cell/nucleus boundary. expansion_steps boolean true Measure intensity in 5 equal-area annular bins dilated 20 µm outward from the cell boundary (distance computed from pixel_size_microns). environment_expansion boolean true Measure a 20 µm pericellular 'Environment' compartment (distance computed automatically from pixel_size_microns). pixel_size_microns number 0.28 Pixel size in microns. estimate_cell_boundary_dist integer 3 For a nucleus with no matching whole-cell ROI, expand the nucleus by this many pixels to make the cell. neighbors integer 0 Number of nearest neighbours used for neighbourhood features. 0 turns them off. gzip_geojson (hidden) boolean true Gzip-compress the output GeoJSON files. Produces .geojson.gz instead of .geojson. dist_threshold number 10.0 Maximum centroid distance in pixels for matching a nucleus to a whole-cell ROI. downsample_factor number 1.0 Downsample factor applied to the image and masks before measurement (1 = no downsampling). tile_size integer 2048 Tile size for large image measurement calculations. tile_overlap integer 200 Tile overlap region in pixels. Should encompass typical cell size. geometry_checkpoint_dir string Directory for resumable polygon-extraction checkpoints. geometry_batch_size integer 2000 Cells per polygon-extraction batch, and the checkpoint granularity.

docs.title: enable_measurements
docs.text: Set to false to skip intensity and shape measurements. Cell outlines are still written to the GeoJSON. Skipping saves time on large images.

docs.title: percentiles
docs.text: Each value must be between 0 and 100. Requires enable_measurements to be true.

docs.title: erosion_steps
docs.text: Splits each cell (and nucleus) into 5 rings of approximately equal area, from the boundary inward, and measures mean and median intensity in each ring. Requires enable_measurements to be true.

docs.title: expansion_steps
docs.text: Splits the 20 µm zone outside each cell into 5 rings of approximately equal area and measures mean and median intensity in each ring. The distance in pixels is computed from pixel_size_microns. Requires enable_measurements to be true.

docs.title: environment_expansion
docs.text: Measures mean, median, min, max and standard deviation of every channel in the zone from the cell boundary to 20 µm outside it, as one region (Environment_20um). The distance in pixels is computed from pixel_size_microns.

docs.title: neighbors
docs.text: For each cell, the mean of every numeric measurement over its nearest neighbours (up to this number, within 20 µm of the cell centroid) is added as Neighbours: Mean: <measurement>. Typical values: 5-10.

docs.title: gzip_geojson
docs.text: Writes .geojson.gz instead of .geojson. Whole-slide GeoJSON files can exceed 100 GB uncompressed; gzip usually reduces them 10-20 times. The import_large_geojson pipeline reads the compressed files directly.

docs.title: dist_threshold
docs.text: A nucleus and a whole-cell ROI whose centroids are further apart than this are not matched. Unmatched nuclei get a cell boundary made by expanding the nucleus (see estimate_cell_boundary_dist).

docs.title: downsample_factor
docs.text: An integer of 2 or more downsamples the image (block mean) and masks (block max) before measurement. Values below 2 mean no downsampling. Area and length measurements are scaled back to full-resolution units.

docs.title: tile_size
docs.text: Measurements are computed on tiles in parallel. Aim for 2-4 times more tiles than CPUs.

docs.title: tile_overlap
docs.text: Set it to at least the diameter of the largest cell, so every cell is complete in at least one tile.

docs.title: geometry_checkpoint_dir
docs.text: Each completed batch of cell polygons is written here, so a CELLMEASUREMENT task that is killed resumes from the last completed batch. The directory must be outside the Nextflow work directory. Checkpoints are not deleted automatically. Leave unset to turn checkpointing off.

docs.title: geometry_batch_size
docs.text: Smaller batches are checkpointed more often but add overhead. A killed task loses at most one batch per worker.

docs.title: Report options
docs.text:
Parameters used for segmentation report generation.

Parameters for the segmentation QC report.

Parameter Type Default Description generate_report boolean false Generate segmentation report.

docs.title: generate_report
docs.text: Set to true to write an HTML QC report per sample. The report is most complete when enable_measurements is true.

docs.title: Mask smoothing options
docs.text:
Parameters for optional mask smoothing before cell measurement.

Enable mask smoothing to reduce polygon complexity in segmentation masks. This can prevent StackOverflowError in QuPath's GeoJSON export when cell ROIs have overly complex/jagged boundaries.

Parameter Type Default Description smooth_masks (hidden) boolean false Enable mask smoothing before cell measurement. smooth_method (hidden) string: morphological, shapely morphological Smoothing algorithm: 'morphological' (disk close+open) or 'shapely' (Douglas-Peucker polygon simplification). smooth_kernel_size (hidden) integer 2 Disk radius in pixels for morphological smoothing. smooth_n_workers (hidden) integer 8 Number of worker processes for mask smoothing. smooth_chunksize (hidden) integer 200 Number of labels each smoothing worker processes at a time. smooth_tolerance (hidden) number 1 Douglas-Peucker tolerance in pixels for shapely smoothing. smooth_min_area (hidden) number 0 Minimum polygon area in pixels² kept after shapely smoothing.

docs.title: smooth_masks
docs.text: Smooths the label masks before cell measurement to reduce the number of polygon vertices. Use it if QuPath fails with StackOverflowError when exporting or loading the GeoJSON. Choose the method with smooth_method.

docs.title: smooth_method
docs.text: morphological applies a binary close then open with a disk of radius smooth_kernel_size. shapely simplifies each cell outline with the Douglas-Peucker algorithm (tolerance smooth_tolerance), which reduces the vertex count directly.

docs.title: smooth_kernel_size
docs.text: Larger values give smoother outlines but can merge neighbouring cells.

docs.title: smooth_n_workers
docs.text: Set it to the number of CPUs allocated to the SMOOTHMASKS task.

docs.title: smooth_chunksize
docs.text: Use larger values for many small cells and smaller values for fewer large cells.

docs.title: smooth_tolerance
docs.text: Higher values give simpler outlines with fewer vertices. Start with 1.

docs.title: smooth_min_area
docs.text: Removes fragments created by simplification. 0 keeps every cell.

docs.title: Institutional config options
docs.text:
Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.

The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

Parameter Type Default Description custom_config_version (hidden) string master Git commit id for Institutional configs. custom_config_base (hidden) string https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/configs/master Base directory for Institutional configs. config_profile_name (hidden) string Institutional config name. config_profile_description (hidden) string Institutional config description. config_profile_contact (hidden) string Institutional config contact information. config_profile_url (hidden) string Institutional config URL link.

docs.title: custom_config_base
docs.text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

docs.title: Generic options
docs.text:
Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.

These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as ~/.nextflow/config.

Parameter Type Default Description version (hidden) boolean false Display version and exit. publish_dir_mode (hidden) string: symlink, rellink, link, copy, copyNoFollow, move copy Method used to save pipeline results to output directory. email_on_fail (hidden) string Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails. plaintext_email (hidden) boolean false Send plain-text email instead of HTML. monochrome_logs (hidden) boolean false Do not use coloured log outputs. hook_url (hidden) string Incoming hook URL for messaging service validate_params (hidden) boolean true Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime pipelines_testdata_base_path (hidden) string https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/test-datasets/ Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files deepcell_cache_dir string Base directory for caching DeepCell/CellSAM model weights. The current username is appended automatically. container_cache_dir string Directory for the Apptainer/Singularity image cache. Set this on any cluster where $HOME has a quota.

docs.title: publish_dir_mode
docs.text: The Nextflow publishDir option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See Nextflow docs for details.

docs.title: email_on_fail
docs.text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

docs.title: hook_url
docs.text: Incoming hook URL for messaging service. Currently, MS Teams and Slack are supported.

docs.title: deepcell_cache_dir
docs.text: Set this to redirect the DeepCell model cache away from the home directory. The current username is resolved at runtime and appended, so models are cached at {deepcell_cache_dir}/{username}/.deepcell/models/. Set to null to use $HOME instead.

docs.title: container_cache_dir
docs.text: Sets apptainer.cacheDir and singularity.cacheDir, so converted .img files are written here rather than under the work directory. This covers only half of a pull: Apptainer unpacks the OCI layers it converts from into $APPTAINER_CACHEDIR (default ~/.apptainer/cache), which Nextflow cannot set because it pulls images from its own process rather than from a task. Export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR and SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR to the same filesystem before launching; the pipeline errors at startup if this parameter is set without them.

docs.title: Resource profiles
docs.text:
The resource profiles run every task as a Slurm job. Combine one with a container profile, for example -profile apptainer,medium.

All resource profiles:

  • submit CPU tasks to the regular partition and GPU tasks (process_gpu) to gpuq with --gres=gpu:1 --constraint=Ampere
  • give GPU tasks the --nv (Apptainer, Singularity) or --gpus all (Docker) container option
  • set a time limit of 48 hours per task
  • submit at most 10 jobs at a time (queueSize = 10), one every 10 seconds
  • multiply memory by the attempt number, so a retried task gets twice the memory

The partition names and GPU constraint are those of WEHI's Milton cluster. On another cluster, write your own profile or override queue and clusterOptions.

docs.title: Which profile
docs.text:
Profile Use for Target node small images up to 150 GB Milton sml (28 cores, 113 GB) medium images up to 300 GB Milton med/il (28 or 48 cores, 491 GB) large images up to 600 GB Milton lrg (64 cores, 1498 GB) wehi_small dense samples on sml nodes Milton sml (28 cores, 113 GB) wehi_med dense samples on med/il nodes Milton med/il (28 or 48 cores, 491 GB) wehi_large very dense samples (millions of cells) Milton lrg (64 cores, 1498 GB)

Memory use depends more on the number of cells than on the file size. The wehi_* profiles request most of a node and suit images with many cells. See Large and dense images.

docs.title: Samplesheet
docs.text: Pass the samplesheet with --input. It can be a CSV file with a header row, or a YAML list. Each row is one image.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column Required Type Default Description sample yes string Sample name. Must be unique in the samplesheet and contain no spaces. Used as the prefix of every output file. Must match ^\S+$. run_backsub no boolean false Run background subtraction before segmentation. COMET OME-TIFF only. run_mesmer no boolean false Segment with Mesmer. At most one of run_mesmer, run_cellpose and run_cellsam can be true per row. run_cellpose no boolean false Segment with Cellpose (patched, through sopa). At most one of run_mesmer, run_cellpose and run_cellsam can be true per row. run_cellsam no boolean false Segment with CellSAM. At most one of run_mesmer, run_cellpose and run_cellsam can be true per row. tiff yes string (file-path) Path to the input image: a COMET OME-TIFF or a multi-channel MIBI TIFF. The path cannot contain spaces. Must match ^\S+\.tiff?$. nuclear_channel no string Name of the nuclear channel, e.g. DAPI. Required when a segmenter is selected. Must match ^[^"':,]+$. membrane_channels no string Names of the membrane channels, separated by ':', e.g. CD45:HLA I. Required when a segmenter is selected. Several channels are combined into one with combine_method. Must match ^[^"':,]+(:[^"':,]+)*$.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• sample must be unique.
  • At most one of run_mesmer, run_cellpose and run_cellsam can be true in a row.
  • At least one run_* column must be true. A row with only run_backsub runs background subtraction only.
  • run_backsub works only on COMET OME-TIFF files.
  • nuclear_channel takes one channel name. membrane_channels takes one or more names separated by :. When there is more than one membrane channel, they are combined with combine_method (default max).
  • Write channel names without quotes. They can contain spaces, but not ", ', : or ,. They must match the channel names in the image exactly.
  • File paths must not contain spaces.

docs.title: CSV example
docs.text:
sample,run_backsub,run_mesmer,run_cellpose,run_cellsam,tiff,nuclear_channel,membrane_channels
slide1,true,false,true,false,/data/slide1.ome.tiff,DAPI,CD45:Pan-Cytokeratin
slide2,false,true,false,false,/data/slide2.ome.tiff,DAPI,HLA I
slide3,true,false,false,false,/data/slide3.ome.tiff,,

slide3 runs background subtraction only.

docs.title: YAML example
docs.text:
- sample: slide1
  run_backsub: true
  run_cellpose: true
  tiff: /data/slide1.ome.tiff
  nuclear_channel: DAPI
  membrane_channels: CD45:Pan-Cytokeratin
- sample: slide2
  run_mesmer: true
  tiff: /data/slide2.ome.tiff
  nuclear_channel: DAPI
  membrane_channels: HLA I

Columns that are left out take their default (false for the run_* columns).
